"""Regression tests for publish-lib exit statuses."""

import json
from argparse import Namespace
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import Mock

import pytest

from charmcraft.application.commands import store as store_commands


def _library(
    tmp_path,
    *,
    name="example",
    lib_id="example-lib-id",
    api=0,
    patch=1,
    content_hash="local-hash",
):
    """Build the local library information consumed by PublishLibCommand."""
    return SimpleNamespace(
        charm_name="mycharm",
        lib_name=name,
        full_name=f"charms.mycharm.v{api}.{name}",
        lib_id=lib_id,
        api=api,
        patch=patch,
        content=(
            f'LIBID = "{lib_id}"\nLIBAPI = {api}\nLIBPATCH = {patch}\n'
        ),
        content_hash=content_hash,
        path=tmp_path / f"{name}.py",
    )


def _tip(*, lib_id="example-lib-id", api=0, patch=1, content_hash="remote-hash"):
    """Build the Charmhub tip corresponding to a local library."""
    return SimpleNamespace(
        lib_id=lib_id,
        api=api,
        patch=patch,
        content_hash=content_hash,
    )


def _command_harness(monkeypatch, tmp_path, libraries, tips):
    """Create a publish-lib command with all store and filesystem I/O mocked."""
    services = SimpleNamespace(
        project=SimpleNamespace(name="mycharm", dirpath=tmp_path)
    )

    # Avoid requiring a fully configured application service factory; run() is the
    # public command operation under test and only needs the project service here.
    command = object.__new__(store_commands.PublishLibCommand)
    command._services = services

    store = Mock()
    store.get_libraries_tips.return_value = tips

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        store_commands.utils,
        "get_libs_from_tree",
        Mock(return_value=libraries),
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", Mock(return_value=store))
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        store_commands.env, "get_store_config", Mock(return_value=object())
    )

    emit_message = Mock()
    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands.emit, "message", emit_message)

    return command, store, emit_message


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("local_patch", "remote_patch", "local_hash", "remote_hash"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            1,
            2,
            "local-hash",
            "remote-hash",
            id="libpatch-went-backwards",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            1,
            1,
            "local-hash",
            "remote-hash",
            id="libpatch-not-bumped-for-changed-content",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_publish_lib_returns_nonzero_when_library_validation_fails(
    monkeypatch,
    tmp_path,
    local_patch,
    remote_patch,
    local_hash,
    remote_hash,
):
    """A rejected library must make the command unsuccessful."""
    library = _library(
        tmp_path,
        patch=local_patch,
        content_hash=local_hash,
    )
    tips = {
        (library.lib_id, library.api): _tip(
            patch=remote_patch,
            content_hash=remote_hash,
        )
    }
    command, store, emit_message = _command_harness(
        monkeypatch, tmp_path, [library], tips
    )

    exit_code = command.run(Namespace(library=None, format=None))

    assert exit_code not in (None, 0)
    store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()
    emit_message.assert_called()


def test_publish_lib_success_remains_successful(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """A valid LIBPATCH bump is published without a failure exit status."""
    library = _library(tmp_path, patch=2, content_hash="new-local-hash")
    tips = {
        (library.lib_id, library.api): _tip(
            patch=1,
            content_hash="old-remote-hash",
        )
    }
    command, store, _ = _command_harness(
        monkeypatch, tmp_path, [library], tips
    )

    exit_code = command.run(Namespace(library=None, format=None))

    assert exit_code in (None, 0)
    store.create_library_revision.assert_called_once()


def test_publish_lib_mixed_results_return_nonzero(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """A later successful publication must not hide an earlier failure."""
    invalid = _library(
        tmp_path,
        name="invalid",
        lib_id="invalid-lib-id",
        patch=1,
    )
    valid = _library(
        tmp_path,
        name="valid",
        lib_id="valid-lib-id",
        patch=2,
        content_hash="valid-new-hash",
    )
    tips = {
        (invalid.lib_id, invalid.api): _tip(
            lib_id=invalid.lib_id,
            patch=2,
            content_hash="invalid-remote-hash",
        ),
        (valid.lib_id, valid.api): _tip(
            lib_id=valid.lib_id,
            patch=1,
            content_hash="valid-old-hash",
        ),
    }
    command, store, _ = _command_harness(
        monkeypatch,
        tmp_path,
        [invalid, valid],
        tips,
    )

    exit_code = command.run(Namespace(library=None, format=None))

    assert exit_code not in (None, 0)
    store.create_library_revision.assert_called_once_with(
        "mycharm",
        valid.lib_id,
        valid.api,
        valid.patch,
        valid.content,
        valid.content_hash,
    )


def test_publish_lib_json_output_also_returns_nonzero_on_failure(
    monkeypatch, tmp_path
):
    """Programmatic output must not accidentally discard the failure status."""
    library = _library(tmp_path, patch=1)
    tips = {
        (library.lib_id, library.api): _tip(
            patch=2,
            content_hash="remote-hash",
        )
    }
    command, store, emit_message = _command_harness(
        monkeypatch, tmp_path, [library], tips
    )

    exit_code = command.run(Namespace(library=None, format="json"))

    assert exit_code not in (None, 0)
    store.create_library_revision.assert_not_called()
    emit_message.assert_called_once()
    output = json.loads(emit_message.call_args.args[0])
    assert isinstance(output, list)
    assert len(output) == 1

"""
Tests for Store.list filtering of live and soft-deleted items.
"""

import pytest

from . import key
from .test_backends import get_posixfs_test_backend

from borgstore.store import ItemInfo, Store


LEVELS_CONFIG = {"zero/": [0], "one/": [1], "two/": [2]}


@pytest.fixture()
def posixfs_store_created(tmp_path):
    store = Store(backend=get_posixfs_test_backend(tmp_path), levels=LEVELS_CONFIG)
    store.create()
    try:
        yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def names(store, namespace, *, deleted=False):
    return [info.name for info in store.list(namespace, deleted=deleted)]


def test_list_separates_live_and_deleted_at_all_nesting_levels(posixfs_store_created):
    """deleted=False and deleted=True must return disjoint, filtered listings."""
    k0, k1, k2 = key(0), key(1), key(2)
    values = {k0: b"value0", k1: b"value1", k2: b"value2"}

    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        for namespace in ("zero", "one", "two"):
            for item_key, value in values.items():
                store.store(f"{namespace}/{item_key}", value)

            store.move(f"{namespace}/{k0}", delete=True)
            store.move(f"{namespace}/{k2}", delete=True)

            # Omitting deleted must have the same meaning as deleted=False.
            assert list(store.list(namespace)) == [
                ItemInfo(name=k1, exists=True, size=len(values[k1]), directory=False)
            ]
            assert names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == [k1]

            # Only soft-deleted items are returned, with their .del suffix removed.
            assert list(store.list(namespace, deleted=True)) == [
                ItemInfo(name=k0, exists=True, size=len(values[k0]), directory=False),
                ItemInfo(name=k2, exists=True, size=len(values[k2]), directory=False),
            ]


def test_list_distinguishes_live_and_deleted_copies_of_same_key(posixfs_store_created):
    """A replacement live item must not hide or join its soft-deleted predecessor."""
    namespace = "zero"
    item_key = key(0)
    full_key = f"{namespace}/{item_key}"
    old_value = b"old"
    replacement_value = b"replacement"

    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(full_key, old_value)
        store.move(full_key, delete=True)
        store.store(full_key, replacement_value)

        assert list(store.list(namespace)) == [
            ItemInfo(name=item_key, exists=True, size=len(replacement_value), directory=False)
        ]
        assert list(store.list(namespace, deleted=True)) == [
            ItemInfo(name=item_key, exists=True, size=len(old_value), directory=False)
        ]


def test_list_deleted_empty_results_and_undelete_transition(posixfs_store_created):
    namespace = "zero"
    item_key = key(0)
    full_key = f"{namespace}/{item_key}"
    value = b"value"

    with posixfs_store_created as store:
        store.store(full_key, value)
        assert names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == [item_key]
        assert names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == []

        store.move(full_key, delete=True)
        assert names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == []
        assert list(store.list(namespace, deleted=True)) == [
            ItemInfo(name=item_key, exists=True, size=len(value), directory=False)
        ]

        store.move(full_key, undelete=True)
        assert names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == [item_key]
        assert names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == []

"""Regression tests for safe filenames for multi-base charms."""

import pathlib
import zipfile
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

import charmcraft.services.package as package_module
from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


def _make_platform_package_service(
    service_factory,
    project_dir: pathlib.Path,
    platform: str,
    architecture: str,
    *,
    base: str | None = None,
) -> services.PackageService:
    """Create a package service for a single-platform charm."""
    project_data = {
        "name": "mysql-router-k8s",
        "type": "charm",
        "summary": "MySQL Router",
        "description": "MySQL Router operator for Kubernetes",
        "platforms": {platform: None},
        "parts": {},
    }
    if base is not None:
        project_data["base"] = base

    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(project_data)
    build_info = BuildInfo(
        platform=platform,
        build_on=architecture,
        build_for=architecture,
        base=BaseName(name="ubuntu", version="22.04"),
    )
    return services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=project_dir,
        build_plan=[build_info],
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("platform", "architecture"),
    [
        ("ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "amd64"),
        ("ubuntu@22.04:arm64", "arm64"),
    ],
)
def test_multi_base_charm_filename_contains_no_colon(
    new_path,
    service_factory,
    platform,
    architecture,
):
    """Multi-base shorthand platforms must produce upload-safe charm names."""
    package_service = _make_platform_package_service(
        service_factory, new_path, platform, architecture
    )

    charm_path = package_service.get_charm_path(new_path)

    assert charm_path.parent == new_path
    assert charm_path.name.startswith("mysql-router-k8s_")
    assert charm_path.name.endswith(".charm")
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name


def test_multi_base_charm_filenames_remain_distinct(new_path, service_factory):
    """Sanitizing must not make the amd64 and arm64 packages overwrite each other."""
    amd64_service = _make_platform_package_service(
        service_factory, new_path, "ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "amd64"
    )
    arm64_service = _make_platform_package_service(
        service_factory, new_path, "ubuntu@22.04:arm64", "arm64"
    )

    amd64_path = amd64_service.get_charm_path(new_path)
    arm64_path = arm64_service.get_charm_path(new_path)

    assert amd64_path.name != arm64_path.name
    assert ":" not in amd64_path.name
    assert ":" not in arm64_path.name


def test_charm_filename_without_colon_is_unchanged(new_path, service_factory):
    """Platforms already safe for artifact uploads retain their existing names."""
    package_service = _make_platform_package_service(
        service_factory,
        new_path,
        "amd64",
        "amd64",
        base="ubuntu@22.04",
    )

    assert package_service.get_charm_path(new_path) == (
        new_path / "mysql-router-k8s_amd64.charm"
    )


def test_pack_creates_colon_free_charm_and_records_its_path(
    new_path,
    service_factory,
):
    """The packed artifact itself, not just its computed path, must be safe."""
    package_service = _make_platform_package_service(
        service_factory, new_path, "ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "amd64"
    )
    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload")
    dest_dir = new_path / "artifacts"
    dest_dir.mkdir()

    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, dest_dir)

    assert len(packages) == 1
    charm_path = packages[0]
    assert charm_path.parent == dest_dir
    assert charm_path.is_file()
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name
    with zipfile.ZipFile(charm_path) as charm_zip:
        assert charm_zip.read("payload.txt") == b"charm payload"

    recorded_packages = (
        new_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt"
    ).read_text().splitlines()
    assert recorded_packages == [charm_path.name]
    assert all(":" not in name for name in recorded_packages)


def test_build_plan_fallback_also_removes_colons(
    monkeypatch,
    new_path,
    service_factory,
):
    """The legacy build-plan filename path must be safe as well."""
    package_service = _make_platform_package_service(
        service_factory, new_path, "ubuntu@22.04:amd64", "amd64"
    )
    matching_build = BuildInfo(
        platform="ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
        build_on="amd64",
        build_for="amd64",
        base=BaseName(name="ubuntu", version="22.04"),
    )

    class StubPlanner:
        def get_build_plan(self):
            return [matching_build]

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        models.CharmcraftBuildPlanner,
        "model_validate",
        lambda *args, **kwargs: StubPlanner(),
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        package_module.utils,
        "get_os_platform",
        lambda: SimpleNamespace(system="ubuntu", release="22.04"),
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        package_module.util, "get_host_architecture", lambda: "amd64"
    )
    package_service._platform = None

    charm_path = package_service.get_charm_path(new_path)

    assert charm_path.name.endswith(".charm")
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name

import io

import pytest

from csv2md.table import Table


def format_row(cells, widths):
    return '| ' + ' | '.join(
        cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(cells, widths)
    ) + ' |'


def test_issue_example_escapes_pipes_without_double_escaping():
    csv_input = (
        '"a","b"\n'
        '"foo","bar"\n'
        '"test|with|pipe|symbol","baz"\n'
        '"test\\|with\\|pipe\\|symbol","baz"\n'
        '"test|with|escaped|pipe","baz"'
    )

    # Widths describe the visible cell contents. The backslash used to escape
    # a pipe is Markdown syntax and does not add to the visible width.
    widths = [37, 3]
    escaped_pipes = 'test\\|with\\|pipe\\|symbol'
    expected = '\n'.join([
        format_row(['a', 'b'], widths),
        format_row(['-' * 37, '-' * 3], widths),
        format_row(['foo', 'bar'], widths),
        format_row([escaped_pipes, 'baz'], widths),
        # Input that was already correctly escaped must remain unchanged.
        format_row([escaped_pipes, 'baz'], widths),
        format_row(['test|with|escaped|pipe', 'baz'], widths),
    ])

    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_input))

    assert table.markdown() == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('value', 'escaped'),
    [
        ('|', '\\|'),
        ('a|b|c', 'a\\|b\\|c'),
        ('|leading', '\\|leading'),
        ('trailing|', 'trailing\\|'),
        ('a||b', 'a\\|\\|b'),
        ('already\\|escaped', 'already\\|escaped'),
        ('entity|pipe', 'entity|pipe'),
        ('C:\\temp\\file', 'C:\\temp\\file'),
        ('', ''),
    ],
)
def test_pipe_escaping_edge_cases(value, escaped):
    table = Table([[value], ['x']])
    width = max(len(value), len('x'))
    expected = '\n'.join([
        format_row([escaped], [width]),
        format_row(['-' * width], [width]),
        format_row(['x'], [width]),
    ])

    assert table.markdown() == expected


def test_escaping_preserves_aligned_column_formatting():
    table = Table([
        ['a|b', 'header'],
        ['x', 'y'],
    ])
    widths = [3, 6]
    expected = '\n'.join([
        format_row(['a\\|b', 'header'], widths),
        format_row([':-:', '-----:'], widths),
        format_row(['x', 'y'], widths),
    ])

    assert table.markdown(
        center_aligned_columns=[0],
        right_aligned_columns=[1],
    ) == expected


def test_escaping_preserves_default_header_formatting():
    table = Table([['a|b', 'c']])
    widths = [3, 1]
    expected = '\n'.join([
        format_row(['a', 'b'], widths),
        format_row(['-' * 3, '-'], widths),
        format_row(['a\\|b', 'c'], widths),
    ])

    assert table.markdown(no_header_row=True) == expected


def test_repeated_rendering_does_not_escape_pipes_again():
    table = Table([
        ['a|b', 'already\\|escaped'],
        ['c|d', 'e|f'],
    ])

    first_rendering = table.markdown()

    assert table.markdown() == first_rendering

from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders


def test_in_place_merge_with_dict_matches_issue_example():
    response = MutableHeaders()
    original_response = response

    response |= {"X-Header": "string"}

    assert response is original_response
    assert repr(response) == "MutableHeaders({'x-header': 'string'})"
    assert response["X-Header"] == "string"
    assert response["x-header"] == "string"
    assert response.raw == [(b"x-header", b"string")]


def test_in_place_merge_is_equivalent_to_update():
    updates = {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Header-3": "string-3",
        "X-Existing": "new-value",
    }
    via_update = MutableHeaders({"X-Existing": "old-value", "X-Keep": "kept"})
    via_operator = MutableHeaders({"X-Existing": "old-value", "X-Keep": "kept"})

    via_update.update(updates)
    via_operator |= updates

    assert via_operator.raw == via_update.raw
    assert dict(via_operator) == {
        "x-existing": "new-value",
        "x-keep": "kept",
        "x-header-1": "string-1",
        "x-header-2": "string-2",
        "x-header-3": "string-3",
    }


def test_merge_operator_returns_an_independent_mutable_headers_instance():
    original = MutableHeaders({"X-Existing": "old", "X-Keep": "kept"})
    original_raw = original.raw.copy()

    merged = original | {"x-existing": "new", "X-Added": "added"}

    assert isinstance(merged, MutableHeaders)
    assert merged is not original
    assert original.raw == original_raw
    assert dict(original) == {"x-existing": "old", "x-keep": "kept"}
    assert dict(merged) == {
        "x-existing": "new",
        "x-keep": "kept",
        "x-added": "added",
    }

    # The returned headers must not share subsequent mutations with the source.
    merged["X-Keep"] = "changed"
    merged["X-Merged-Only"] = "value"
    assert original["X-Keep"] == "kept"
    assert "X-Merged-Only" not in original

    original["X-Original-Only"] = "value"
    assert "X-Original-Only" not in merged


def test_in_place_merge_replaces_duplicates_case_insensitively():
    headers = MutableHeaders(
        raw=[
            (b"x-duplicate", b"first"),
            (b"x-other", b"unchanged"),
            (b"x-duplicate", b"second"),
        ]
    )

    headers |= {"X-Duplicate": "updated"}

    assert headers.getlist("X-Duplicate") == ["updated"]
    assert headers.items() == [
        ("x-duplicate", "updated"),
        ("x-other", "unchanged"),
    ]


def test_merge_with_empty_dict_preserves_contents_and_operator_semantics():
    headers = MutableHeaders({"X-Header": "value"})
    original_headers = headers

    headers |= {}

    assert headers is original_headers
    assert headers.items() == [("x-header", "value")]

    merged = headers | {}

    assert isinstance(merged, MutableHeaders)
    assert merged is not headers
    assert merged == headers
    assert merged.items() == [("x-header", "value")]


def test_in_place_merge_updates_scope_backed_headers():
    raw_headers = [(b"content-type", b"text/plain")]
    scope = {"headers": raw_headers}
    headers = MutableHeaders(scope=scope)

    headers |= {"X-Header": "string"}

    assert scope["headers"] == [
        (b"content-type", b"text/plain"),
        (b"x-header", b"string"),
    ]
    assert headers["X-Header"] == "string"

"""Regression tests for using additional scoring metrics in cross-validation."""

import numpy
import pytest
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

from skore import CrossValidationReporter, cross_validate
from skore.item.cross_validation_aggregation_item import (
    CrossValidationAggregationItem,
)


def regression_data():
    """Return a small, deterministic regression dataset."""
    X = numpy.arange(60, dtype=float).reshape(30, 2)
    y = 1.0 + 2.0 * X[:, 0] - X[:, 1]
    return X, y


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "scoring, expected_score_keys",
    [
        (
            ["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
            {
                "test_neg_mean_absolute_error",
                "test_r2",
                "test_explained_variance",
            },
        ),
        (("r2",), {"test_r2"}),
    ],
)
def test_cross_validate_supports_list_and_tuple_scoring_with_project(
    in_memory_project, scoring, expected_score_keys
):
    """The public API accepts extra scores when results are put in a project."""
    X, y = regression_data()

    # Simulate a project that already contains an earlier, default-scored run.
    cross_validate(LinearRegression(), X, y, cv=3, project=in_memory_project)
    reporter = cross_validate(
        LinearRegression(),
        X,
        y,
        cv=3,
        project=in_memory_project,
        scoring=scoring,
    )

    assert isinstance(reporter, CrossValidationReporter)
    assert expected_score_keys <= reporter.cv_results.keys()
    for key in expected_score_keys:
        assert len(reporter.cv_results[key]) == 3


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "original_scoring, new_scoring",
    [
        # Adding metrics must not make the stored runs impossible to aggregate.
        (
            ["r2"],
            ["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
        ),
        # A tuple produces test_r2, whereas the equivalent string produces
        # test_score; aggregation must tolerate that difference between runs.
        ("r2", ("r2",)),
        # This also covers adding extra scores to an existing default-scored run.
        (
            None,
            ["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_aggregation_supports_runs_with_different_score_columns(
    in_memory_project, original_scoring, new_scoring
):
    """Runs with different serialized score columns can still be aggregated."""
    X, y = regression_data()

    for scoring in (original_scoring, new_scoring):
        reporter = CrossValidationReporter(
            LinearRegression(), X, y, cv=3, scoring=scoring
        )
        in_memory_project.put("cv", reporter)

    versions = in_memory_project.get_item_versions("cv")
    assert len(versions) == 2

    # In particular, this must not raise pandas' "cannot reindex on an axis
    # with duplicate labels" error while exploding the results.
    aggregated = CrossValidationAggregationItem.factory(versions)
    assert isinstance(aggregated, CrossValidationAggregationItem)

"""Regression tests for multi-base charm artifact filenames."""

import pathlib
import zipfile

import pytest
from craft_application.models import BuildInfo
from craft_providers.bases import BaseName

from charmcraft import models, services
from charmcraft.application.main import APP_METADATA


def _make_multi_base_package_service(
    new_path: pathlib.Path,
    service_factory,
    platform: str,
) -> services.PackageService:
    """Create a package service for the multi-base charm from the bug report."""
    project = models.PlatformCharm.model_validate(
        {
            "name": "mysql-router-k8s",
            "summary": "MySQL Router charm",
            "description": "A multi-base charm used to test package filenames.",
            "type": "charm",
            "base": None,
            "build-base": None,
            "platforms": {
                "ubuntu@22.04:amd64": None,
                "ubuntu@22.04:arm64": None,
            },
            "parts": {},
        }
    )
    architecture = platform.rsplit(":", 1)[1]
    build_plan = [
        BuildInfo(
            platform=platform,
            build_on=architecture,
            build_for=architecture,
            base=BaseName("ubuntu", "22.04"),
        )
    ]
    package_service = services.PackageService(
        app=APP_METADATA,
        project=project,
        services=service_factory,
        project_dir=new_path,
        build_plan=build_plan,
    )
    service_factory.package = package_service
    return package_service


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("platform", "expected_name"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            "ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
            "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm",
            id="amd64",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            "ubuntu@22.04:arm64",
            "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-arm64.charm",
            id="arm64",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_multi_base_charm_path_does_not_contain_colon(
    new_path,
    service_factory,
    platform,
    expected_name,
):
    """A shorthand multi-base platform must produce an upload-safe filename."""
    package_service = _make_multi_base_package_service(
        new_path, service_factory, platform
    )

    charm_path = package_service.get_charm_path(new_path)

    assert charm_path == new_path / expected_name
    assert ":" not in charm_path.name


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("platform", "expected_name"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            "ubuntu@22.04:amd64",
            "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-amd64.charm",
            id="amd64",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            "ubuntu@22.04:arm64",
            "mysql-router-k8s_ubuntu@22.04-arm64.charm",
            id="arm64",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_pack_multi_base_charm_creates_sanitized_artifact(
    new_path,
    service_factory,
    platform,
    expected_name,
):
    """Packing must create and record the sanitized path, not merely display it."""
    package_service = _make_multi_base_package_service(
        new_path, service_factory, platform
    )
    prime_dir = new_path / "prime"
    prime_dir.mkdir()
    (prime_dir / "payload.txt").write_text("charm payload", encoding="utf-8")

    packages = package_service.pack(prime_dir, new_path)

    expected_path = new_path / expected_name
    assert packages == [expected_path]
    assert expected_path.is_file()
    assert ":" not in expected_path.name
    with zipfile.ZipFile(expected_path) as charm_file:
        assert charm_file.read("payload.txt") == b"charm payload"

    # Consumers use this file to locate artifacts for subsequent CI steps.
    output_packages = (new_path / ".charmcraft_output_packages.txt").read_text(
        encoding="utf-8"
    )
    assert output_packages == f"{expected_name}\n"
    assert ":" not in output_packages

import pytest

from ucumvert import PintUcumRegistry


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def ureg():
    return PintUcumRegistry()


def assert_same_quantity(actual, expected_unit):
    """Compare using actual's registry; from_ucum may use the app registry."""
    converted = actual.to(expected_unit)
    assert converted.magnitude == pytest.approx(1.0)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ucum_code", "expected_unit", "unprefixed_unit", "expected_factor"),
    [
        (
            "m[IU]",
            "milliinternational_unit",
            "international_unit",
            1e-3,
        ),
        (
            "m[IU]/L",
            "milliinternational_unit / liter",
            "international_unit / liter",
            1e-3,
        ),
        (
            "k[IU]/L",
            "kilointernational_unit / liter",
            "international_unit / liter",
            1e3,
        ),
    ],
)
def test_prefixed_international_unit(
    ureg, ucum_code, expected_unit, unprefixed_unit, expected_factor
):
    """A UCUM prefix must prefix IU, not become a separate multiplied unit."""
    actual = ureg.from_ucum(ucum_code)

    assert str(actual.units) == expected_unit
    assert actual.magnitude == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert_same_quantity(actual, expected_unit)

    # Also check the meaning of the prefix, independently of its display name.
    converted = actual.to(unprefixed_unit)
    assert converted.magnitude == pytest.approx(expected_factor)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("ucum_code", "expected_unit"),
    [
        ("[IU]/L", "international_unit / liter"),
        # The dot explicitly requests multiplication by metres. This must remain
        # distinct from m[IU], where m is the milli prefix.
        ("m.[IU]/L", "meter * international_unit / liter"),
    ],
)
def test_international_unit_without_a_prefix_is_unchanged(
    ureg, ucum_code, expected_unit
):
    actual = ureg.from_ucum(ucum_code)

    assert actual.magnitude == pytest.approx(1.0)
    assert_same_quantity(actual, expected_unit)

"""Regression tests for cleaning and deleting suspect/corrupt file copies."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest

from alpenhorn.daemon.update import UpdateableNode
from alpenhorn.db import (
    ArchiveAcq,
    ArchiveFile,
    ArchiveFileCopy,
    ArchiveFileCopyRequest,
    StorageGroup,
    StorageNode,
)


def _make_clean_copies():
    """Create a node with one copy in each possible has_file state."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    copies = {}
    for has_file in ("Y", "M", "X", "N"):
        file = ArchiveFile.create(name=f"File{has_file}", acq=acq, size_b=1234)
        copies[has_file] = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
            node=node, file=file, has_file=has_file, wants_file="Y"
        )

    return copies


def _make_daemon_node(storage_node):
    """Make an UpdateableNode with controlled I/O for testing its update queries."""
    node = UpdateableNode.__new__(UpdateableNode)
    node.db = storage_node
    node.io = MagicMock()
    node.io.fifo = "node-fifo"
    node.io.before_update.return_value = True

    node._queue = MagicMock()
    node._queue.fifo_size.return_value = 0
    node._io_happened = False
    node._updated = False
    return node


def _make_storage_node():
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="DaemonGroup")
    return StorageNode.create(
        name="DaemonNode",
        group=group,
        storage_type="F",
        min_avail_gb=0.0,
        avail_gb=100.0,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("now, clean_goal", [(False, "M"), (True, "N")])
def test_clean_excludes_bad_copies_by_default(clidb, cli, now, clean_goal):
    """Without --include-bad, only healthy copies are scheduled for cleaning."""
    copies = _make_clean_copies()

    args = ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--force"]
    if now:
        args.append("--now")
    cli(0, args)

    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(copies["Y"].id).wants_file == clean_goal

    # Suspect and corrupt copies must be left alone by a normal clean.
    for has_file in ("M", "X"):
        assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(copies[has_file].id).wants_file == "Y"

    # A copy which is not present is never a cleaning candidate.
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(copies["N"].id).wants_file == "Y"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("now, clean_goal", [(False, "M"), (True, "N")])
def test_clean_include_bad(clidb, cli, now, clean_goal):
    """--include-bad schedules suspect and corrupt copies as well as healthy ones."""
    copies = _make_clean_copies()

    args = ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--force", "--include-bad"]
    if now:
        args.append("--now")
    cli(0, args)

    for has_file in ("Y", "M", "X"):
        assert (
            ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(copies[has_file].id).wants_file == clean_goal
        )

    # Including bad copies must not make absent copies cleaning candidates.
    assert ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(copies["N"].id).wants_file == "Y"


def test_update_delete_includes_released_bad_copies(dbtables):
    """The daemon deletes released M/X copies, but not absent or wanted copies."""
    storage_node = _make_storage_node()
    node = _make_daemon_node(storage_node)
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    copies = {}
    for has_file, wants_file in (
        ("Y", "Y"),
        ("Y", "M"),
        ("Y", "N"),
        ("M", "Y"),
        ("M", "M"),
        ("M", "N"),
        ("X", "Y"),
        ("X", "M"),
        ("X", "N"),
        ("N", "N"),
    ):
        file = ArchiveFile.create(
            name=f"file_{has_file}_{wants_file}", acq=acq, size_b=1234
        )
        copies[(has_file, wants_file)] = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
            node=storage_node,
            file=file,
            has_file=has_file,
            wants_file=wants_file,
        )

    node.update_delete()

    deleted_ids = {
        copy.id
        for delete_call in node.io.delete.call_args_list
        for copy in delete_call.args[0]
    }
    expected_ids = {
        copies[(has_file, "N")].id for has_file in ("Y", "M", "X")
    }

    assert deleted_ids == expected_ids


def test_update_does_not_check_released_suspect_copies(dbtables):
    """A suspect copy released for deletion is deleted, not integrity checked."""
    storage_node = _make_storage_node()
    node = _make_daemon_node(storage_node)
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    copies = {}
    for wants_file in ("Y", "M", "N"):
        file = ArchiveFile.create(name=f"suspect_{wants_file}", acq=acq)
        copies[wants_file] = ArchiveFileCopy.create(
            node=storage_node,
            file=file,
            has_file="M",
            wants_file=wants_file,
        )

    # Isolate integrity-check selection from the other update operations.
    with patch(
        "alpenhorn.daemon.update.auto_import.update_observer"
    ), patch.object(node, "update_free_space"), patch.object(
        node, "update_delete"
    ), patch("alpenhorn.daemon.update.RemoteNode"):
        node.update()

    checked_ids = {
        check_call.args[0].id for check_call in node.io.check.call_args_list
    }

    # Other suspect copies still need checking; the released one does not.
    assert checked_ids == {copies["Y"].id, copies["M"].id}
    assert copies["N"].id not in checked_ids


def test_update_delete_bad_copy_with_pending_transfer(dbtables):
    """Bad copies remain protected when they are sources for pending transfers."""
    storage_node = _make_storage_node()
    node = _make_daemon_node(storage_node)
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")
    group = storage_node.group

    file = ArchiveFile.create(name="pending_transfer", acq=acq)
    ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=storage_node, file=file, has_file="X", wants_file="N"
    )
    ArchiveFileCopyRequest.create(
        node_from=storage_node,
        group_to=group,
        file=file,
        completed=False,
        cancelled=False,
    )

    node.update_delete()

    node.io.delete.assert_not_called()

"""Regression tests for publish-lib's exit status."""

import argparse
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import MagicMock

import pytest

from charmcraft.application.commands import store as store_commands
from charmcraft.store.models import Library


CHARM_NAME = "testcharm"
API = 0


def _remote_library(
    name: str,
    *,
    patch: int,
    content_hash: str = "remote-content-hash",
) -> Library:
    """Build the library metadata returned by Charmhub."""
    return Library(
        lib_id=f"library-id-{name}",
        lib_name=name,
        charm_name=CHARM_NAME,
        api=API,
        patch=patch,
        content="content currently in Charmhub",
        content_hash=content_hash,
    )


def _local_library(
    remote: Library,
    *,
    patch: int,
    content_hash: str = "new-local-content-hash",
) -> SimpleNamespace:
    """Build the local library metadata returned by library discovery."""
    return SimpleNamespace(
        lib_id=remote.lib_id,
        lib_name=remote.lib_name,
        charm_name=remote.charm_name,
        full_name=f"charms.{remote.charm_name}.v{remote.api}.{remote.lib_name}",
        api=remote.api,
        patch=patch,
        content="new local library content",
        content_hash=content_hash,
        path=None,
    )


def _run_publish_lib(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    remote_libraries: list[Library],
    local_libraries: list[SimpleNamespace],
    output_format: str | None = None,
):
    """Run PublishLibCommand with Charmhub and local discovery mocked."""
    store = MagicMock(name="store")
    store.get_libraries_info.return_value = remote_libraries

    monkeypatch.setattr(store_commands, "Store", MagicMock(return_value=store))
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        store_commands.utils,
        "get_libs_from_tree",
        lambda charm_name: local_libraries,
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        store_commands.utils,
        "get_lib_info",
        MagicMock(side_effect=local_libraries),
    )

    project = SimpleNamespace(name=CHARM_NAME, charm_name=CHARM_NAME)
    project.get = lambda: project
    services = SimpleNamespace(project=project)
    command = store_commands.PublishLibCommand(
        {"app": SimpleNamespace(), "services": services}
    )

    parsed_args = argparse.Namespace(library=None, format=output_format)
    result = command.run(parsed_args)
    return result, store


@pytest.mark.parametrize("output_format", [None, "json"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("local_patch", "remote_patch", "remote_hash", "local_hash"),
    [
        # LIBPATCH was not bumped after changing the library.
        (4, 4, "remote-hash", "local-hash"),
        # LIBPATCH went backwards, as in the issue's reproduction steps.
        (3, 4, "remote-hash", "local-hash"),
        # LIBPATCH was bumped even though the library content did not change.
        (5, 4, "unchanged-hash", "unchanged-hash"),
    ],
)
def test_publish_lib_analysis_failure_returns_nonzero(
    monkeypatch,
    emitter,
    output_format,
    local_patch,

    backing_list = headers.raw
    updates = {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Header-3": "string-3",
        "X-Header-N": "string-N",
    }

    headers |= updates

    assert headers.raw is backing_list
    assert dict(headers) == {
        "content-type": "text/plain",
        "x-header-1": "string-1",
        "x-header-2": "string-2",
        "x-header-3": "string-3",
        "x-header-n": "string-N",
    }
    assert updates == {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Header-3": "string-3",
        "X-Header-N": "string-N",
    }


def test_mutable_headers_ior_has_update_semantics():
    initial = [
        (b"x-duplicate", b"old-1"),
        (b"x-duplicate", b"old-2"),
        (b"x-other", b"keep-1"),
        (b"x-other", b"keep-2"),
    ]
    changes = {"X-Duplicate": "updated", "X-New": "new-value"}

    expected = MutableHeaders(raw=initial.copy())
    expected.update(changes)

    headers = MutableHeaders(raw=initial.copy())
    original = headers
    headers |= changes

    assert headers is original
    assert headers.items() == expected.items()
    assert headers.getlist("x-duplicate") == ["updated"]
    assert headers.getlist("x-other") == ["keep-1", "keep-2"]
    assert headers["x-new"] == "new-value"


def test_mutable_headers_or_returns_new_independent_instance():
    original = MutableHeaders(
        raw=[
            (b"x-existing", b"old-1"),
            (b"x-existing", b"old-2"),
            (b"x-original", b"unchanged"),
        ]
    )

    merged = original | {"X-Existing": "new", "X-Added": "value"}

    assert isinstance(merged, MutableHeaders)
    assert merged is not original
    assert merged.raw is not original.raw
    assert original.items() == [
        ("x-existing", "old-1"),
        ("x-existing", "old-2"),
        ("x-original", "unchanged"),
    ]
    assert merged.items() == [
        ("x-existing", "new"),
        ("x-original", "unchanged"),
        ("x-added", "value"),
    ]

    merged["x-added"] = "changed"
    original["x-original"] = "also-changed"
    assert "x-added" not in original
    assert merged["x-original"] == "unchanged"

import io

import pytest

from csv2md.table import Table


def _row(cells, widths):
    """Build an expected Markdown row using the project's table format."""
    return "| " + " | ".join(
        cell.ljust(width) for cell, width in zip(cells, widths)
    ) + " |"


def test_csv_pipe_characters_are_escaped_and_column_widths_stay_aligned():
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(
        '"a","b"\n'
        '"foo","bar"\n'
        '"test|with|pipe|symbol","baz"\n'
    ))

    escaped_item = r"test\|with\|pipe\|symbol"
    widths = [24, 3]

    assert table.markdown() == "\n".join([
        _row(["a", "b"], widths),
        _row(["-" * 24, "-" * 3], widths),
        _row(["foo", "bar"], widths),
        _row([escaped_item, "baz"], widths),
    ])


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("value", "escaped"),
    [
        ("|", r"\|"),
        ("||", r"\|\|"),
        ("a|b|c", r"a\|b\|c"),
        ("|leading", r"\|leading"),
        ("trailing|", r"trailing\|"),
    ],
)
def test_all_pipes_are_escaped_including_leading_and_trailing_pipes(value, escaped):
    width = len(escaped)

    assert Table([[value]]).markdown() == "\n".join([
        _row([escaped], [width]),
        _row(["-" * width], [width]),
    ])


def test_escaped_widths_are_used_for_alignment_separators():
    table = Table([
        ["h|h", "r", "c"],
        ["x", "long", "mid"],
    ])
    widths = [4, 4, 3]

    assert table.markdown(
        right_aligned_columns=[1],
        center_aligned_columns=[2],
    ) == "\n".join([
        _row([r"h\|h", "r", "c"], widths),
        _row(["----", "---:", ":-:"], widths),
        _row(["x", "long", "mid"], widths),
    ])


def test_pipes_are_escaped_when_no_header_row_is_supplied():
    table = Table([
        ["left|right", "2"],
        ["x", "10"],
    ])
    widths = [11, 2]

    assert table.markdown(no_header_row=True) == "\n".join([
        _row(["a", "b"], widths),
        _row(["-" * 11, "-" * 2], widths),
        _row([r"left\|right", "2"], widths),
        _row(["x", "10"], widths),
    ])


def test_escaping_does_not_mutate_cells_or_change_on_repeated_rendering():
    cells = [["a|b", "plain"]]
    table = Table(cells)

    first_rendering = table.markdown()

    assert r"a\|b" in first_rendering
    assert cells == [["a|b", "plain"]]
    assert table.cells == [["a|b", "plain"]]
    assert table.markdown() == first_rendering


def test_html_pipe_entities_are_left_unchanged():
    value = "test|with|escaped|pipe"

    output = Table([[value]]).markdown()

    assert value in output
    assert r"\|" not in output

"""
Tests for Store.list filtering of normal and soft-deleted items.
"""

import pytest

from borgstore.store import ItemInfo, Store


LEVELS_CONFIG = {"zero/": [0], "one/": [1], "two/": [2]}
K0 = "00000000"
K1 = "11000001"
K2 = "ff000002"


@pytest.fixture()
def store(tmp_path):
    # Use only the local filesystem backend; no external services are needed.
    store = Store(url=(tmp_path / "store").as_uri(), levels=LEVELS_CONFIG)
    store.create()
    try:
        with store:
            yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def listed_names(store, namespace, *, deleted):
    return sorted(info.name for info in store.list(namespace, deleted=deleted))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("namespace", ["zero", "one", "two"])
def test_list_returns_only_items_in_requested_state(store, namespace):
    """The filter must also be applied while recursing through nesting directories."""
    values = {K0: b"value0", K1: b"value1", K2: b"value2"}
    for key, value in values.items():
        store.store(f"{namespace}/{key}", value)

    store.move(f"{namespace}/{K0}", delete=True)
    store.move(f"{namespace}/{K2}", delete=True)

    # deleted=False, including its default form, lists only normal items.
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == [K1]
    assert [info.name for info in store.list(namespace)] == [K1]

    # deleted=True lists only soft-deleted items, not the normal item as well.
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == [K0, K2]


def test_list_deleted_empty_all_deleted_and_undelete(store):
    namespace = "zero"
    # Listing a namespace that does not exist raises ObjectNotFound on posixfs.
    # Create the empty namespace so these assertions exercise an empty listing.
    store.backend.mkdir(namespace)

    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == []
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == []

    store.store(f"{namespace}/{K0}", b"value0")
    store.store(f"{namespace}/{K1}", b"value1")

    # A store without soft-deleted items has nothing to list for deleted=True.
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == [K0, K1]
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == []

    store.move(f"{namespace}/{K0}", delete=True)
    store.move(f"{namespace}/{K1}", delete=True)

    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == []
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == [K0, K1]

    store.move(f"{namespace}/{K0}", undelete=True)

    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == [K0]
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == [K1]

    # Really removing the remaining soft-deleted item removes it from the listing.
    store.delete(f"{namespace}/{K1}", deleted=True)
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=False) == [K0]
    assert listed_names(store, namespace, deleted=True) == []


def test_list_deleted_strips_suffix_and_preserves_item_info(store):
    namespace = "zero"
    value = b"soft-deleted value"
    store.store(f"{namespace}/{K0}", value)
    store.move(f"{namespace}/{K0}", delete=True)

    # Deleted items are presented under their original key, without ".del",
    # while the rest of their ItemInfo remains intact.
    assert list(store.list(namespace, deleted=True)) == [
        ItemInfo(name=K0, exists=True, size=len(value), directory=False)
    ]
    assert list(store.list(namespace, deleted=False)) == []

    values = {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Header-3": "string-3",
        "X-Header-N": "string-N",
    }
    expected = MutableHeaders()
    expected.update(values)

    headers = MutableHeaders()
    original = headers
    headers |= values

    assert headers is original
    assert headers.items() == expected.items()
    assert dict(headers) == {key.lower(): value for key, value in values.items()}
    assert values == {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Header-3": "string-3",
        "X-Header-N": "string-N",
    }


def test_mutable_headers_inplace_merge_replaces_case_insensitively():
    backing = [
        (b"x-existing", b"old"),
        (b"x-existing", b"duplicate"),
        (b"x-other", b"keep"),
    ]
    headers = MutableHeaders(raw=backing)
    original = headers

    headers |= {"X-Existing": "new", "X-Added": "value"}

    assert headers is original
    assert headers.getlist("x-existing") == ["new"]
    assert headers.raw == [
        (b"x-existing", b"new"),
        (b"x-other", b"keep"),
        (b"x-added", b"value"),
    ]

"""Regression tests for using multiple scorers with cross-validation aggregation."""

import numpy
import pytest
from sklearn.ensemble import HistGradientBoostingRegressor

from skore import CrossValidationReporter, cross_validate
from skore.item.cross_validation_aggregation_item import CrossValidationAggregationItem
from skore.item.cross_validation_item import CrossValidationItem


CV = 3


def make_data():
    """Return a deterministic regression dataset with well-defined test scores."""
    rng = numpy.random.default_rng(42)
    X = rng.normal(size=(36, 3))
    y = 3 * X[:, 0] - 2 * X[:, 1] + X[:, 2] + rng.normal(scale=0.1, size=36)
    return X, y


def run_twice_with_project(project, scoring):
    """Run twice so that the project has to aggregate multiple CV versions."""
    X, y = make_data()
    reporters = []

    for _ in range(2):
        reporter = cross_validate(
            HistGradientBoostingRegressor(max_iter=5, random_state=0),
            X,
            y,
            cv=CV,
            project=project,
            scoring=scoring,
        )
        assert isinstance(reporter, CrossValidationReporter)
        reporters.append(reporter)

    return reporters


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("scoring", "expected_score_keys"),
    [
        pytest.param(
            ["neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"],
            {
                "test_neg_mean_absolute_error",
                "test_r2",
                "test_explained_variance",
            },
            id="multiple-scores-list-from-issue",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            ("neg_mean_absolute_error", "r2", "explained_variance"),
            {
                "test_neg_mean_absolute_error",
                "test_r2",
                "test_explained_variance",
            },
            id="multiple-scores-tuple",
        ),
        pytest.param(("r2",), {"test_r2"}, id="single-score-tuple-from-issue"),
        pytest.param(["r2"], {"test_r2"}, id="single-score-list"),
        pytest.param("r2", {"test_r2"}, id="single-score-string-control"),
        pytest.param(None, {"test_score"}, id="default-scoring-control"),
    ],
)
def test_cross_validate_scoring_survives_project_aggregation(
    in_memory_project, scoring, expected_score_keys
):
    """Lists and tuples of scorers must work when versions are aggregated.

    In particular, constructing the aggregation plot must not attempt to
    reindex exploded pandas Series with duplicate labels. Requested scores
    must also remain present in both the results and the aggregation plot.
    """
    reporters = run_twice_with_project(in_memory_project, scoring)

    for reporter in reporters:
        assert expected_score_keys.issubset(reporter.cv_results)
        for key in expected_score_keys:
            assert len(reporter.cv_results[key]) == CV

    # Exercise the same item factories used by project storage explicitly, so
    # the test also checks aggregation independently of the storage backend.
    items = [CrossValidationItem.factory(reporter) for reporter in reporters]
    aggregated = CrossValidationAggregationItem.factory(items)

    # Silently skipping or emptying the plot is not a valid fix: aggregation
    # should still produce a useful visualization containing every score.
    assert aggregated.plot is not None
    assert aggregated.plot.data
    serialized_plot = aggregated.plot.to_json()
    for key in expected_score_keys:
        assert key in serialized_plot

def test_mutable_headers_inplace_merge_with_dict():
    headers = MutableHeaders()
    original = headers

    headers |= {"X-Header": "string"}

    assert headers is original
    assert repr(headers) == "MutableHeaders({'x-header': 'string'})"
    assert dict(headers) == {"x-header": "string"}
    assert headers.raw == [(b"x-header", b"string")]


def test_mutable_headers_inplace_merge_updates_case_insensitively():
    raw = [
        (b"x-existing", b"first"),
        (b"x-existing", b"second"),
        (b"x-other", b"keep"),
    ]
    headers = MutableHeaders(raw=raw)

    headers |= {"X-Existing": "updated", "X-Added": "value"}

    assert headers.items() == [
        ("x-existing", "updated"),
        ("x-other", "keep"),
        ("x-added", "value"),
    ]
    assert headers.getlist("X-Existing") == ["updated"]
    assert raw == [
        (b"x-existing", b"updated"),
        (b"x-other", b"keep"),
        (b"x-added", b"value"),
    ]


def test_mutable_headers_merge_returns_independent_instance():
    original = MutableHeaders({"X-One": "1", "X-Two": "2"})

    merged = original | {"x-two": "updated", "X-Three": "3"}

    assert isinstance(merged, MutableHeaders)
    assert merged is not original
    assert original.items() == [("x-one", "1"), ("x-two", "2")]
    assert merged.items() == [
        ("x-one", "1"),
        ("x-two", "updated"),
        ("x-three", "3"),
    ]

    merged["X-One"] = "changed"
    original["X-Four"] = "4"
    assert original["X-One"] == "1"
    assert "x-four" not in merged


def test_mutable_headers_merge_operators_match_update():
    values = {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Header-3": "string-3",
        "Existing": "new-value",
    }
    expected = MutableHeaders({"Existing": "old-value"})
    expected.update(values)
    actual = MutableHeaders({"Existing": "old-value"})

    actual |= values

    assert actual.raw == expected.raw
    assert dict(actual) == dict(expected)
    assert repr(actual) == repr(expected)


def test_mutable_headers_merge_with_empty_dict():
    headers = MutableHeaders({"X-Header": "value"})
    original = headers
    original_raw = headers.raw[:]

    headers |= {}

    assert headers is original
    assert headers.raw == original_raw

    merged = headers | {}
    assert merged is not headers
    assert merged == headers
    assert merged.raw == headers.raw
    assert merged.raw is not headers.raw

import io

import pytest

from csv2md.table import Table


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_and_recalculates_column_widths():
    table = Table([
        ['a', 'b'],
        ['foo', 'bar'],
        ['test|with|pipe|symbol', 'baz'],
    ])

    expected = '\n'.join([
        '| a                        | b   |',
        '| ------------------------ | --- |',
        '| foo                      | bar |',
        r'| test\|with\|pipe\|symbol | baz |',
    ])

    assert table.markdown() == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('value', 'escaped'),
    [
        ('|', r'\|'),
        ('a||', r'a\|\|'),
        ('|start|', r'\|start\|'),
    ],
)
def test_markdown_escapes_every_pipe_including_edges_and_adjacent_pipes(value, escaped):
    table = Table([['h'], [value]])

    data_row = table.markdown().splitlines()[-1]

    assert data_row == '| ' + escaped + ' |'


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_in_header_cells():
    table = Table([['h|'], ['x']])

    expected = '\n'.join([
        r'| h\| |',
        '| --- |',
        '| x   |',
    ])

    assert table.markdown() == expected


def test_markdown_alignment_separators_use_escaped_widths():
    table = Table([
        ['a', 'bb'],
        ['x|y', 'z'],
    ])

    expected = '\n'.join([
        '| a    | bb |',
        '| :--: | -: |',
        r'| x\|y | z  |',
    ])

    assert table.markdown(center_aligned_columns=[0], right_aligned_columns=[1]) == expected


def test_markdown_with_default_headers_escapes_pipes_in_data():
    table = Table([['x|y', 'z']])

    expected = '\n'.join([
        '| a    | b |',
        '| ---- | - |',
        r'| x\|y | z |',
    ])

    assert table.markdown(no_header_row=True) == expected


def test_parse_csv_pipe_escaping_is_non_destructive_and_repeatable():
    csv_text = (
        '"name","note"\n'
        '"a|b","plain"\n'
        '"c","d|e"\n'
    )
    original_cells = [
        ['name', 'note'],
        ['a|b', 'plain'],
        ['c', 'd|e'],
    ]
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(csv_text))

    expected = '\n'.join([
        '| name | note  |',
        '| ---- | ----- |',
        r'| a\|b | plain |',
        r'| c    | d\|e  |',
    ])

    assert table.cells == original_cells
    assert table.markdown() == expected
    assert table.markdown() == expected
    assert table.cells == original_cells


def test_html_pipe_entities_are_left_unchanged():
    value = 'test|with|escaped|pipe'
    table = Table([['a'], [value]])

    markdown = table.markdown()

    assert value in markdown
    assert markdown.count('|') == 3
    assert r'\|' not in markdown

"""Regression tests for cleaning suspect and corrupt file copies."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, PropertyMock, patch

from click.testing import CliRunner

from alpenhorn.cli.node.clean import clean
from alpenhorn.daemon.update import UpdateableNode
from alpenhorn.db import ArchiveAcq, ArchiveFileCopy


def _wants_file(copy):
    """Return the current database value of wants_file for copy."""
    return ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(copy.id).wants_file


def _make_clean_copies(prefix, node, archivefile, archivefilecopy):
    """Make one wanted copy in each possible has_file state."""
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name=prefix)
    copies = {}

    for has_file in ("Y", "X", "M", "N"):
        file_ = archivefile(name=f"{prefix}-{has_file}", acq=acq, size_b=1024)
        copies[has_file] = archivefilecopy(
            file=file_, node=node, has_file=has_file, wants_file="Y"
        )

    return copies


def _invoke_clean(node_name, *options):
    """Invoke the clean command without interactive confirmation."""
    return CliRunner().invoke(
        clean,
        [node_name, "--archive-ok", "--now", "--force", *options],
    )


def test_update_delete_includes_released_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(
    dbtables, simplenode, queue, archivefile, archivefilecopy
):
    """The daemon releases Y, X, and M copies, but never absent copies."""
    # Keep the node above its minimum so that only explicitly released copies
    # (wants_file=N) are deletion candidates.
    simplenode.min_avail_gb = 0.0
    simplenode.avail_gb = 1.0
    simplenode.save()

):

        ("deferred", "M"),

"""Regression tests for Store.list soft-deletion filtering."""

import pytest

from borgstore.store import ItemInfo, Store

from . import key
from .test_backends import get_posixfs_test_backend


LEVELS_CONFIG = {"zero/": [0], "nested/": [1]}


@pytest.fixture()
def posixfs_store(tmp_path):
    store = Store(
        backend=get_posixfs_test_backend(tmp_path),
        levels=LEVELS_CONFIG,
    )
    store.create()
    try:
        with store:
            yield store
    finally:
        store.destroy()


def list_names(store, namespace, *, deleted):
    return [info.name for info in store.list(namespace, deleted=deleted)]


def test_list_separates_normal_and_soft_deleted_items(posixfs_store):
    namespace = "zero"
    live_keys = [key(0), key(2)]
    deleted_keys = [key(1), key(3)]
    values = {
        key(0): b"live-zero",
        key(1): b"deleted-one",
        key(2): b"live-two",
        key(3): b"deleted-three",
    }

    for item_key, value in values.items():
        posixfs_store.store(f"{namespace}/{item_key}", value)
    for item_key in deleted_keys:
        posixfs_store.move(f"{namespace}/{item_key}", delete=True)

    # Omitting the argument retains the default of listing only live items.
    assert [info.name for info in posixfs_store.list(namespace)] == live_keys
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=False) == live_keys

    # deleted=True means exclusively soft-deleted items, not live items too.
    deleted_infos = list(posixfs_store.list(namespace, deleted=True))
    assert deleted_infos == [
        ItemInfo(
            name=item_key,
            exists=True,
            size=len(values[item_key]),
            directory=False,
        )
        for item_key in deleted_keys
    ]


def test_list_deleted_filter_through_item_lifecycle(posixfs_store):
    namespace = "zero"
    item_key = key(0)
    namespaced_key = f"{namespace}/{item_key}"

    posixfs_store.store(namespaced_key, b"value")
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=False) == [item_key]
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=True) == []

    posixfs_store.move(namespaced_key, delete=True)
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=False) == []
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=True) == [item_key]

    posixfs_store.move(namespaced_key, undelete=True)
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=False) == [item_key]
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=True) == []

    posixfs_store.delete(namespaced_key)
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=False) == []
    assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=True) == []


def test_list_deleted_filter_applies_at_flat_and_nested_levels(posixfs_store):
    live_key = key(0)
    deleted_key = key(1)

    for namespace in ("zero", "nested"):
        posixfs_store.store(f"{namespace}/{live_key}", b"live")
        posixfs_store.store(f"{namespace}/{deleted_key}", b"soft deleted")
        posixfs_store.move(f"{namespace}/{deleted_key}", delete=True)

        assert list_names(posixfs_store, namespace, deleted=False) == [live_key]

        deleted_infos = list(posixfs_store.list(namespace, deleted=True))
        assert [info.name for info in deleted_infos] == [deleted_key]
        assert deleted_infos[0].size == len(b"soft deleted")
        assert deleted_infos[0].exists
        assert not deleted_infos[0].directory

import pytest

from textual.app import App
from textual.widget import Widget


@pytest.mark.parametrize("direction", ["before", "after"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("child_reference", "anchor_reference"),
    [
        ("widget", "widget"),
        ("index", "index"),
        ("widget", "index"),
        ("index", "widget"),
    ],
)
@pytest.mark.parametrize("child_index", [0, 1, 2])
async def test_move_child_relative_to_itself_is_noop(
    direction: str,
    child_reference: str,
    anchor_reference: str,
    child_index: int,
) -> None:
    """A child can identify itself with either a widget or its index."""
    widgets = [Widget(id=f"child-{index}") for index in range(3)]
    parent = Widget(*widgets)

    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        await pilot.app.mount(parent)
        assert list(parent.children) == widgets

        child = child_index if child_reference == "index" else widgets[child_index]
        anchor = (
            child_index if anchor_reference == "index" else widgets[child_index]
        )

        parent.move_child(child, **{direction: anchor})

        assert list(parent.children) == widgets


async def test_move_only_child_relative_to_itself_is_noop() -> None:
    """Self-moves must also be valid when there are no sibling widgets."""
    child = Widget(id="only-child")
    parent = Widget(child)

    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        await pilot.app.mount(parent)

        for direction in ("before", "after"):
            parent.move_child(child, **{direction: child})
            assert list(parent.children) == [child]

            parent.move_child(0, **{direction: 0})
            assert list(parent.children) == [child]


async def test_self_move_noop_does_not_disable_other_moves() -> None:
    """Handling self-moves specially must not affect ordinary reordering."""
    widgets = [Widget(id=f"child-{index}") for index in range(4)]
    parent = Widget(*widgets)

    async with App().run_test() as pilot:
        await pilot.app.mount(parent)

        parent.move_child(widgets[1], after=widgets[1])
        assert list(parent.children) == widgets

        parent.move_child(widgets[0], after=widgets[2])
        assert list(parent.children) == [
            widgets[1],
            widgets[2],
            widgets[0],
            widgets[3],
        ]

        parent.move_child(widgets[3], before=widgets[1])
        assert list(parent.children) == [
            widgets[3],
            widgets[1],
            widgets[2],
            widgets[0],
        ]

from starlette.datastructures import MutableHeaders
from starlette.responses import Response


def test_mutable_headers_inplace_merge_with_dict_issue_example():
    headers = MutableHeaders()

    headers |= {"X-Header": "string"}

    assert repr(headers) == "MutableHeaders({'x-header': 'string'})"
    assert headers["X-Header"] == "string"
    assert headers.raw == [(b"x-header", b"string")]


def test_mutable_headers_inplace_merge_multiple_headers():
    values = {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Header-3": "string-3",
        "X-Header-N": "string-N",
    }
    original_values = values.copy()
    headers = MutableHeaders()

    headers |= values

    assert dict(headers) == {key.lower(): value for key, value in values.items()}
    assert values == original_values


def test_mutable_headers_inplace_merge_is_update_on_same_object():
    initial_raw = [
        (b"content-type", b"text/plain"),
        (b"x-token", b"old"),
        (b"x-token", b"duplicate"),
    ]
    headers = MutableHeaders(raw=initial_raw.copy())
    alias = headers
    values = {
        "X-Header-1": "string-1",
        "X-Header-2": "string-2",
        "X-Token": "new",
    }

    expected = MutableHeaders(raw=initial_raw.copy())
    expected.update(values)

    headers |= values

    # |= must update the existing object, just like update(), rather than
    # replacing it with a separate merged object.
    assert headers is alias
    assert headers.items() == expected.items()
    assert headers.raw == expected.raw
    assert headers["Content-Type"] == "text/plain"
    assert headers.getlist("x-token") == ["new"]
    assert headers["X-Header-1"] == "string-1"
    assert headers["X-Header-2"] == "string-2"


def test_mutable_headers_or_returns_independent_merged_copy():
    original = MutableHeaders({"X-Existing": "old"})
    original_raw = original.raw.copy()
    values = {"X-New": "new", "x-existing": "updated"}
    original_values = values.copy()

    merged = original | values

    assert isinstance(merged, MutableHeaders)
    assert merged is not original
    assert dict(merged) == {"x-existing": "updated", "x-new": "new"}
    assert merged.getlist("x-existing") == ["updated"]

    # The merge must not modify either operand.
    assert original.raw == original_raw
    assert dict(original) == {"x-existing": "old"}
    assert values == original_values

    # The returned object must not share mutable header storage with the source.
    merged["X-Merged-Only"] = "merged"
    original["X-Original-Only"] = "original"
    assert "x-merged-only" not in original
    assert "x-original-only" not in merged


def test_mutable_headers_merge_with_empty_dict():
    original = MutableHeaders({"A": "1"})
    original_raw = original.raw.copy()
    alias = original

    merged = original | {}

    assert isinstance(merged, MutableHeaders)
    assert merged is not original
    assert merged.raw == original_raw
    assert merged.raw is not original.raw

    original |= {}

    assert original is alias
    assert original.raw == original_raw


def test_response_headers_object_supports_inplace_dict_merge():
    response = Response(headers={"X-Existing": "old"})
    headers = response.headers

    # Response.headers is a read-only property, so augmented assignment cannot
    # be applied to the property itself. Its MutableHeaders value can be merged.
    headers |= {"X-Header": "string", "X-Existing": "new"}

    assert response.headers is headers
    assert response.headers["X-Header"] == "string"
    assert response.headers["X-Existing"] == "new"
    assert (b"x-header", b"string") in response.raw_headers
    assert (b"x-existing", b"new") in response.raw_headers
    assert (b"x-existing", b"old") not in response.raw_headers

import io

from csv2md.table import Table


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_in_headers_and_cells_and_uses_escaped_widths():
    cells = [
        ['h|h', 'r'],
        ['x', 'a|b'],
    ]

    expected = (
        '| h\\|h | r    |\n'
        '| ---- | ---- |\n'
        '| x    | a\\|b |'
    )

    assert Table(cells).markdown() == expected


def test_markdown_escapes_leading_trailing_and_consecutive_pipes():
    table = Table([
        ['h'],
        ['|a||b|'],
        ['plain'],
    ])

    rows = table.markdown().splitlines()

    assert rows[2] == '| \\|a\\|\\|b\\| |'


def test_markdown_alignment_separators_account_for_escaped_pipes():
    table = Table([
        ['h', 'r'],
        ['a|b', 'xyz'],
    ])

    expected = (
        '| h    | r   |\n'
        '| :--: | --: |\n'
        '| a\\|b | xyz |'
    )

    assert table.markdown(center_aligned_columns=[0], right_aligned_columns=[1]) == expected


def test_markdown_escapes_pipes_when_generating_default_headers():
    table = Table([
        ['a|b', 'xyz'],
    ])

    expected = (
        '| a    | b   |\n'
        '| ---- | --- |\n'
        '| a\\|b | xyz |'
    )

    assert table.markdown(no_header_row=True) == expected


def test_parse_csv_escapes_pipes_only_when_rendering_and_leaves_html_entities_unchanged():
    source = (
        'a,b\n'
        '"x|y",z\n'
        '"|",w\n'
    )
    table = Table.parse_csv(io.StringIO(source))

    assert table.cells == [
        ['a', 'b'],
        ['x|y', 'z'],
        ['|', 'w'],
    ]
    assert table.markdown() == (
        '| a      | b |\n'
        '| ------ | - |\n'
        '| x\\|y   | z |\n'
        '| | | w |'
    )

"""Tests for cleaning and deleting suspect/corrupt file copies."""

from unittest.mock import PropertyMock, patch

import pytest

from alpenhorn.daemon.update import UpdateableNode
from alpenhorn.db import (
    ArchiveAcq,
    ArchiveFile,
    ArchiveFileCopy,
    StorageGroup,
    StorageNode,
)


def _make_copy(node, acq, name, has_file, wants_file="Y"):
    """Create a file and its copy on ``node``."""
    file = ArchiveFile.create(name=name, acq=acq, size_b=1234)
    return ArchiveFileCopy.create(
        node=node,
        file=file,
        has_file=has_file,
        wants_file=wants_file,
    )


def _wants_file(copy):
    """Fetch the current wants_file value from the database."""
    return ArchiveFileCopy.get_by_id(copy.id).wants_file


def test_daemon_deletes_unwanted_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(
    dbtables, simplenode, queue
):
    """The daemon should submit present, unwanted X/M copies for deletion."""
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    expected = {
        state: _make_copy(simplenode, acq, f"delete-{state}", state, "N")
        for state in ("Y", "X", "M")
    }

    # Copies which are still wanted, or which are not present, must not be
    # submitted for deletion.
    not_expected = [
        _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "wanted-Y", "Y", "Y"),
        _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "wanted-X", "X", "Y"),
        _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "wanted-M", "M", "Y"),
        _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "absent", "N", "N"),
    ]

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, simplenode)
    with patch.object(unode.io, "delete") as mock_delete:
        unode.update_delete()

    deleted = [
        copy
        for delete_call in mock_delete.call_args_list
        for copy in delete_call.args[0]
    ]
    deleted_ids = {copy.id for copy in deleted}

    assert deleted_ids == {copy.id for copy in expected.values()}
    assert deleted_ids.isdisjoint({copy.id for copy in not_expected})


def test_daemon_does_not_check_corrupt_copy_it_will_delete(
    dbtables, simplenode, queue
):
    """Only corrupt copies which are still wanted should be checked."""
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    wanted = _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "wanted", "M", "Y")
    deferred = _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "deferred", "M", "M")
    unwanted = _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "unwanted", "M", "N")

    # Suspect copies are not integrity-check candidates in any case.
    suspect = _make_copy(simplenode, acq, "suspect", "X", "Y")

    unode = UpdateableNode(queue, simplenode)
    with (
        patch.object(
            UpdateableNode,
            "idle",
            new_callable=PropertyMock,
            return_value=True,
        ),
        patch.object(unode.io, "before_update", return_value=True),
        patch.object(unode.io, "check") as mock_check,
        patch.object(unode, "update_free_space"),
        patch.object(unode, "update_delete"),
        patch("alpenhorn.daemon.update.auto_import.update_observer"),
        patch("alpenhorn.daemon.update.RemoteNode"),
    ):
        unode.update()

    checked_ids = {
        check_call.args[0].id for check_call in mock_check.call_args_list
    }
    assert checked_ids == {wanted.id, deferred.id}
    assert unwanted.id not in checked_ids
    assert suspect.id not in checked_ids


def test_clean_excludes_bad_copies_by_default(clidb, cli):
    """Without --include-bad, clean retains its original Y-only behaviour."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    good = _make_copy(node, acq, "good", "Y")
    suspect = _make_copy(node, acq, "suspect", "X")
    corrupt = _make_copy(node, acq, "corrupt", "M")
    absent = _make_copy(node, acq, "absent", "N")

    cli(0, ["node", "clean", "NODE", "--force"])

    assert _wants_file(good) == "M"
    assert _wants_file(suspect) == "Y"
    assert _wants_file(corrupt) == "Y"
    assert _wants_file(absent) == "Y"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("extra_args", "expected_goal"),
    [([], "M"), (["--now"], "N")],
)
def test_clean_include_bad_flags_suspect_and_corrupt_copies(
    clidb, cli, extra_args, expected_goal
):
    """--include-bad should clean X/M copies as well as ordinary Y copies."""
    group = StorageGroup.create(name="Group")
    node = StorageNode.create(name="NODE", group=group, storage_type="F")
    acq = ArchiveAcq.create(name="Acq")

    present = [
        _make_copy(node, acq, "good", "Y"),
        _make_copy(node, acq, "suspect", "X"),
        _make_copy(node, acq, "corrupt", "M"),
    ]
    absent = _make_copy(node, acq, "absent", "N")

    cli(
        0,
        [
            "node",
            "clean",
            "NODE",
            "--force",
            "--include-bad",
            *extra_args,
        ],
    )

    assert {_wants_file(copy) for copy in present} == {expected_goal}
    # An absent copy is not a file which can be cleaned from the node.
    assert _wants_file(absent) == "Y"

import pytest

from textual.app import App
from textual.widget import Widget


pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio


async def make_parent(app: App, count: int = 3):
    """Create and mount a parent whose children have a known initial order."""
    children = [Widget(id=f"child-{index}") for index in range(count)]
    parent = Widget(*children)
    await app.mount(parent)
    return parent, children


def assert_order(parent: Widget, expected) -> None:
    """Check the public child order, including that no children were lost."""
    assert list(parent.children) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize("direction", ["before", "after"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("child_index", [0, 1, 2])
async def test_move_widget_before_or_after_itself_is_noop(
    direction: str, child_index: int
) -> None:
    """A widget used as its own positional reference must not be moved."""
    app = App()
    async with app.run_test():
        parent, children = await make_parent(app)
        child = children[child_index]

        parent.move_child(child, **{direction: child})

        assert_order(parent, children)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("direction", ["before", "after"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("child_index", [0, 1, 2, -1])
async def test_move_child_index_before_or_after_same_index_is_noop(
    direction: str, child_index: int
) -> None:
    """The no-op rule also applies when the API is used with indices."""
    app = App()
    async with app.run_test():
        parent, children = await make_parent(app)

        parent.move_child(child_index, **{direction: child_index})

        assert_order(parent, children)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("direction", ["before", "after"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("child_as_index", "reference_as_index"),
    [(False, True), (True, False)],
)
async def test_move_child_before_or_after_itself_with_mixed_references_is_noop(
    direction: str, child_as_index: bool, reference_as_index: bool
) -> None:
    """Widget and index references can denote the same child."""
    app = App()
    async with app.run_test():
        parent, children = await make_parent(app)
        child_index = 1
        child = child_index if child_as_index else children[child_index]
        reference = child_index if reference_as_index else children[child_index]

        parent.move_child(child, **{direction: reference})

        assert_order(parent, children)


async def test_move_only_child_before_and_after_itself_is_noop() -> None:
    """Self-moves must also be harmless when there are no siblings."""
    app = App()
    async with app.run_test():
        parent, children = await make_parent(app, count=1)
        child = children[0]

        parent.move_child(child, before=child)
        parent.move_child(child, after=child)

        assert_order(parent, children)


async def test_self_move_noop_does_not_disable_normal_child_moves() -> None:
    """Genuine moves before and after other children must still reorder them."""
    app = App()
    async with app.run_test():
        parent, children = await make_parent(app, count=4)
        first, second, third, fourth = children

        parent.move_child(first, after=third)
        assert_order(parent, [second, third, first, fourth])

        parent.move_child(fourth, before=second)
        assert_order(parent, [fourth, second, third, first])
