from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import uuid

import pytest

import setuptools_scm
from setuptools_scm import _entrypoints
from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion


_SCHEME_MODULE_SOURCE = '''\
def version_scheme(version):
    return "9.8.7"


def local_scheme(version):
    return "+qualified"


def none_scheme(version):
    return None


not_callable = 42
'''


def _write_scheme_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch, *, nested=False):
    """Create an importable scheme module without installing any entry points."""
    stem = f"ttg_qualified_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    if nested:
        package = tmp_path / stem
        package.mkdir()
        (package / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
        (package / "schemes.py").write_text(
            _SCHEME_MODULE_SOURCE, encoding="utf-8"
        )
        module_name = f"{stem}.schemes"
    else:
        (tmp_path / f"{stem}.py").write_text(
            _SCHEME_MODULE_SOURCE, encoding="utf-8"
        )
        module_name = stem

    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    return module_name


def _no_local_scheme(version):
    return ""


def _fixed_version_scheme(version):
    return "1.2.3"


def _no_result(version):
    return None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("scheme_kind", ["version", "local"])
def test_get_version_accepts_qualified_scheme_names(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch, scheme_kind
):
    module_name = _write_scheme_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch)

    if scheme_kind == "version":
        version_scheme = f"{module_name}:version_scheme"
        local_scheme = _no_local_scheme
        expected = "9.8.7"
    else:
        version_scheme = _fixed_version_scheme
        local_scheme = f"{module_name}:local_scheme"
        expected = "1.2.3+qualified"

    def parse(root, config):
        return ScmVersion("1.0", config=config)

    result = setuptools_scm.get_version(
        root=str(tmp_path),
        parse=parse,
        version_scheme=version_scheme,
        local_scheme=local_scheme,
    )

    assert result == expected


def test_qualified_name_can_reference_a_nested_package_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    module_name = _write_scheme_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch, nested=True)

    result = _entrypoints._call_version_scheme(
        object(),
        "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
        f"{module_name}:version_scheme",
        "fallback",
    )

    assert result == "9.8.7"


def test_qualified_names_work_inside_scheme_lists(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    module_name = _write_scheme_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch)

    result = _entrypoints._call_version_scheme(
        object(),
        "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
        [
            _no_result,
            f"{module_name}:none_scheme",
            f"{module_name}:version_scheme",
        ],
        "fallback",
    )

    assert result == "9.8.7"


def test_invalid_qualified_names_preserve_default_scheme_behavior(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    module_name = _write_scheme_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    missing_module = f"ttg_missing_{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    invalid_schemes = [
        f"{missing_module}:version_scheme",
        f"{module_name}:does_not_exist",
        f"{module_name}:not_callable",
        f"{module_name}:none_scheme",
        f"{module_name}:",
        ":version_scheme",
    ]

    for scheme in invalid_schemes:
        assert (
            _entrypoints._call_version_scheme(
                object(),
                "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
                scheme,
                "fallback",
            )
            == "fallback"
        )


def test_plain_entry_point_names_continue_to_work(monkeypatch):
    class FakeEntryPoint:
        name = "legacy-scheme"

        def load(self):
            return _fixed_version_scheme

    def fake_iter_entry_points(group, name=None):
        assert group == "setuptools_scm.version_scheme"
        assert name == "legacy-scheme"
        return iter([FakeEntryPoint()])

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        _entrypoints, "iter_entry_points", fake_iter_entry_points
    )

    result = _entrypoints._call_version_scheme(
        object(),
        "setuptools_scm.version_scheme",
        "legacy-scheme",
        "fallback",
    )

    assert result == "1.2.3"

import pytest

from checkov.cloudformation.runner import Runner
from checkov.runner_filter import RunnerFilter


CHECK_ID = "CKV_AWS_24"
RESOURCE_TYPE = "AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup"


def _security_group(name, cidr_ip="0.0.0.0/0"):
    return (
        f"  {name}:\n"
        "    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup\n"
        "    Properties:\n"
        "      GroupDescription: Test security group\n"
        "      SecurityGroupIngress:\n"
        "        - IpProtocol: tcp\n"
        "          FromPort: 22\n"
        "          ToPort: 22\n"
        f"          CidrIp: {cidr_ip}\n"
    )


def _run_template(tmp_path, template):
    template_path = tmp_path / "template.yaml"
    template_path.write_text(template, encoding="utf-8")

    report = Runner().run(
        root_folder=None,
        external_checks_dir=None,
        files=[str(template_path)],
        runner_filter=RunnerFilter(framework="all", checks=[CHECK_ID]),
    )

    assert report.get_summary()["parsing_errors"] == 0
    return report


def test_insecure_security_group_fails_without_suppression(tmp_path):
    template = (
        "AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'\n"
        "Resources:\n"
        + _security_group("SecurityGroup")
    )

    report = _run_template(tmp_path, template)

    assert report.skipped_checks == []
    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
    assert report.failed_checks[0].check_id == CHECK_ID
    assert report.failed_checks[0].resource == f"{RESOURCE_TYPE}.SecurityGroup"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "skip_comment",
    [
        "#checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:",
        "#checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24",
        "#checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:SSH access is intentionally open",
    ],
)
def test_skip_comment_before_resource_suppresses_check(tmp_path, skip_comment):
    template = (
        "AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'\n"
        "Resources:\n"
        f"  {skip_comment}\n"
        + _security_group("SecurityGroup")
    )

    report = _run_template(tmp_path, template)

    assert report.failed_checks == []
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    skipped = report.skipped_checks[0]
    assert skipped.check_id == CHECK_ID
    assert skipped.resource == f"{RESOURCE_TYPE}.SecurityGroup"


def test_issue_style_suppression_with_ref_parameter(tmp_path):
    template = (
        "AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'\n"
        "Parameters:\n"
        "  SSHLocation:\n"
        "    Type: String\n"
        "    Default: 0.0.0.0/0\n"
        "Resources:\n"
        "  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:\n"
        + _security_group("SecurityGroup", cidr_ip="!Ref SSHLocation")
    )

    report = _run_template(tmp_path, template)

    assert report.failed_checks == []
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].check_id == CHECK_ID
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == f"{RESOURCE_TYPE}.SecurityGroup"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("suppressed_resource", ["First", "Second"])
def test_suppression_is_scoped_to_the_following_resource(
    tmp_path, suppressed_resource
):
    first_prefix = (
        "  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:Only suppress this resource\n"
        if suppressed_resource == "First"
        else ""
    )
    second_prefix = (
        "  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_24:Only suppress this resource\n"
        if suppressed_resource == "Second"
        else ""
    )
    other_resource = "Second" if suppressed_resource == "First" else "First"

    template = (
        "AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'\n"
        "Resources:\n"
        + first_prefix
        + _security_group("First")
        + second_prefix
        + _security_group("Second")
    )

    report = _run_template(tmp_path, template)

    # A suppression between two resources belongs to the resource that follows
    # it; it must not also suppress findings on the preceding resource.
    assert len(report.skipped_checks) == 1
    assert report.skipped_checks[0].resource == (
        f"{RESOURCE_TYPE}.{suppressed_resource}"
    )
    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
    assert report.failed_checks[0].resource == f"{RESOURCE_TYPE}.{other_resource}"


def test_suppression_for_another_check_does_not_hide_failure(tmp_path):

        "AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'\n"
        "Resources:\n"
        "  #checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_23:This is a different check\n"
        + _security_group("SecurityGroup")
    )

    report = _run_template(tmp_path, template)

    assert report.skipped_checks == []
    assert len(report.failed_checks) == 1
    assert report.failed_checks[0].check_id == CHECK_ID

import importlib

from setuptools_scm import get_version
from setuptools_scm import _entrypoints
from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion


def _write_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch, module_name: str, source: str) -> None:
    (tmp_path / f"{module_name}.py").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(source), encoding="utf-8"
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))
    importlib.invalidate_caches()


def test_get_version_supports_qualified_scheme_without_entry_point(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """A source-tree module can provide version_scheme before installation."""
    package = tmp_path / "_ttg_qualified_project"
    package.mkdir()
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (package / "schemes.py").write_text(
        textwrap.dedent(
            """
            calls = []

            def version_scheme(version):
                calls.append(version)
                return "9.8.7"
            """
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))
    importlib.invalidate_caches()

    def unexpected_entry_point_lookup(group, name):
        raise AssertionError(
            f"a resolved qualified name must not need entry point {group}/{name}"
        )

    monkeypatch.setattr(_entrypoints, "_get_ep", unexpected_entry_point_lookup)

        parsed_versions.append(parsed)
        return parsed

    result = get_version(
        root=str(project),
        parse=fake_parse,
        version_scheme="_ttg_qualified_project.schemes:version_scheme",
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert result == "9.8.7"
    assert len(parsed_versions) == 1

    assert len(schemes.calls) == 1

)
from gspread.worksheet import ValueRange, Worksheet


SPREADSHEET_ID = "spreadsheet-id"
SHEET_TITLE = "Sheet 1"


def value_range_response(values=None):
    return {
        "range": "'Sheet 1'!A1:B2",
        "majorDimension": "ROWS",
        "values": [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]] if values is None else values,
    }


@pytest.fixture
def worksheet_and_client():
    client = Mock()
    client.values_get.return_value = value_range_response()
    client.values_batch_get.return_value = {
        "valueRanges": [value_range_response([["a"]])]
    }
    client.values_update.return_value = {"updatedCells": 1}
    client.values_batch_update.return_value = {"totalUpdatedCells": 1}
    client.fetch_sheet_metadata.return_value = {
        "sheets": [{"properties": {"title": SHEET_TITLE, "sheetId": 0}}]
    }

    worksheet = Worksheet(
        SPREADSHEET_ID,
        client,
        {
            "sheetId": 0,
            "title": SHEET_TITLE,
            "index": 0,
            "gridProperties": {"rowCount": 20, "columnCount": 10},
        },
    )
    return worksheet, client


def test_kwargs_helpers_are_removed_and_public_options_are_explicit():
    # Both spellings are checked: the issue uses the singular name, while the
    # obsolete implementation was named filter_dict_values.
    assert not hasattr(utils, "accepted_kwargs")
    assert not hasattr(utils, "filter_dict_value")
    assert not hasattr(utils, "filter_dict_values")

    required = inspect.Parameter.empty
    expected_signatures = {
        "get_values": [
            ("range_name", None),
            ("major_dimension", None),
            # Keep combine_merged_cells before the former **kwargs options so
            # its existing positional calling convention remains valid.
            ("combine_merged_cells", False),
            ("value_render_option", None),
            ("date_time_render_option", None),
        ],
        "get_all_values": [
            ("major_dimension", None),
            ("value_render_option", None),
            ("date_time_render_option", None),
        ],
        "row_values": [

            ("major_dimension", None),
            ("value_render_option", None),

            ("include_values_in_response", None),
            ("response_value_render_option", None),

            "majorDimension": Dimension.cols,

            "dateTimeRenderOption": DateTimeOption.formatted_string,

def test_get_values_accepts_all_options_positionally_and_still_combines_merges(
    worksheet_and_client,
):
    worksheet, client = worksheet_and_client

    values = worksheet.get_values(
        "A1:B2",
        Dimension.rows,
        False,
        ValueRenderOption.formatted,
        DateTimeOption.serial_number,
    )

    client.values_get.assert_called_once_with(
        SPREADSHEET_ID,
        "'Sheet 1'!A1:B2",
        params={
            "majorDimension": Dimension.rows,
            "valueRenderOption": ValueRenderOption.formatted,
            "dateTimeRenderOption": DateTimeOption.serial_number,
        },
    )
    client.fetch_sheet_metadata.assert_not_called()

        [["top-left", ""], ["", ""]]
    )
    client.fetch_sheet_metadata.return_value = {
        "sheets": [
            {
                "properties": {"title": SHEET_TITLE, "sheetId": 0},
                "merges": [
                    {
                        "startRowIndex": 0,
                        "endRowIndex": 2,
                        "startColumnIndex": 0,
                        "endColumnIndex": 2,
                    }
                ],
            }
        ]

    payload = {"some": "payload", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")

    decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"])

    # Validation ignores the null claim, while decoding still preserves the

    assert decoded == payload

    token = jwt.encode({"some": "payload", "aud": None}, "secret")

    # application requires an audience, an absent aud claim is reported as
    # missing rather than as an invalid claim format.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import setuptools_scm._entrypoints as scheme_entrypoints
from setuptools_scm import get_version


def _git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> None:
    subprocess.run(
        ["git", *args],
        cwd=repo,
        check=True,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )


def _tagged_repo(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    repo.mkdir()
    _git(repo, "init", "--quiet")
    _git(repo, "config", "user.name", "Test User")
    _git(repo, "config", "user.email", "test@example.com")
    _git(repo, "config", "commit.gpgsign", "false")
    (repo / "tracked.txt").write_text("tracked\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _git(repo, "add", "tracked.txt")
    _git(repo, "commit", "--quiet", "-m", "initial commit")
    _git(repo, "tag", "1.2.3")
    return repo


def _import_directory(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> Path:
    directory = tmp_path / "importable"
    directory.mkdir()
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(directory))
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    return directory


def test_get_version_uses_qualified_scheme_without_entry_points(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """A source-importable scheme must not require an installed entry point."""
    import_dir = _import_directory(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    (import_dir / "ttg_custom_scheme.py").write_text(
        "def version_scheme(version):\n"
        "    return 'qualified-' + str(version.tag)\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    repo = _tagged_repo(tmp_path)

    def entry_points_must_not_be_needed(group: str, name: str) -> None:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"qualified scheme unexpectedly used entry-point lookup: {group}/{name}"
        )

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        scheme_entrypoints, "_get_ep", entry_points_must_not_be_needed
    )

    result = get_version(
        root=str(repo),
        version_scheme="ttg_custom_scheme:version_scheme",
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert result == "qualified-1.2.3"


def test_qualified_scheme_supports_dotted_modules_and_scheme_lists(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Qualified names compose with the existing multi-scheme fallback behavior."""
    import_dir = _import_directory(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    package = import_dir / "ttg_scheme_package"
    package.mkdir()
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (package / "schemes.py").write_text(
        "def skip(version):\n"
        "    return None\n"
        "\n"
        "def version_scheme(version):\n"
        "    return 'dotted-list-' + str(version.tag)\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    repo = _tagged_repo(tmp_path)

    result = get_version(
        root=str(repo),
        version_scheme=[
            "ttg_scheme_package.schemes:skip",
            "ttg_scheme_package.schemes:version_scheme",
        ],
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert result == "dotted-list-1.2.3"


def test_plain_entry_point_scheme_names_remain_supported(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """Adding qualified-name loading must not replace entry-point lookup."""
    repo = _tagged_repo(tmp_path)

    result = get_version(
        root=str(repo),
        version_scheme="guess-next-dev",
        local_scheme="no-local-version",
    )

    # guess-next-dev returns the tag itself on an exact, clean tagged commit.
    assert result == "1.2.3"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "scheme_name",
    [
        "ttg_module_that_does_not_exist:version_scheme",
        "ttg_existing_scheme_module:missing_scheme",
    ],
)
def test_unresolvable_qualified_name_falls_back_to_entry_point_lookup(
    tmp_path: Path,
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch,
    scheme_name: str,
) -> None:

    import_dir = _import_directory(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    (import_dir / "ttg_existing_scheme_module.py").write_text(
        "def present_scheme(version):\n"
        "    return 'present'\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    importlib.invalidate_caches()
    repo = _tagged_repo(tmp_path)
    lookups: list[tuple[str, str]] = []

    def fake_get_ep(group: str, name: str):
        lookups.append((group, name))
        return lambda version: "entry-point-fallback"

    result = get_version(
        root=str(repo),
        version_scheme=scheme_name,
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert result == "entry-point-fallback"
    assert lookups == [("setuptools_scm.version_scheme", scheme_name)]

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src
from add_trailing_comma import main


ISSUE_INPUT = (
    "f('long'\n"
    "  'literal')"
)
ISSUE_EXPECTED = (
    "f(\n"
    "    'long'\n"
    "    'literal',\n"
    ")"
)


def assert_fixed_in_one_pass(src, expected):
    actual = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)
    assert actual == expected
    # The result of the first pass must already be fully formatted.
    assert _fix_src(actual, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_multiline_string_literal_call_fixed_in_one_pass():
    assert_fixed_in_one_pass(ISSUE_INPUT, ISSUE_EXPECTED)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        # The intermediate output shown in the issue should need only a comma,
        # rather than another formatting pass.
        (
            "f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal'\n"
            ")",
            ISSUE_EXPECTED,
        ),
        # More than two adjacent literals should behave the same way.
        (
            "f('one'\n"
            "  'two'\n"
            "  'three')",
            "f(\n"
            "    'one'\n"
            "    'two'\n"
            "    'three',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # Calls are not limited to a bare NAME immediately before the paren.
        (
            "obj.method('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "obj.method(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "factory()('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "factory()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "calls[0]('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "calls[0](\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # Indentation should be based on the containing block.
        (
            "if ready:\n"
            "    f('long'\n"
            "      'literal')",
            "if ready:\n"
            "    f(\n"
            "        'long'\n"
            "        'literal',\n"
            "    )",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_string_literal_call_variants(src, expected):
    assert_fixed_in_one_pass(src, expected)


@pytest.mark.parametrize('prefix', ('not ', 'left and '))
def test_parenthesized_string_concatenation_is_not_a_call(prefix):
    # A trailing comma here would create a tuple and change the expression.
    # Only actual calls should receive the new comma.
    src = "value = {}('long'\n  'literal')".format(prefix)
    expected = "value = {}(\n    'long'\n    'literal'\n)".format(prefix)
    assert_fixed_in_one_pass(src, expected)


def test_one_line_adjacent_string_literals_are_unchanged():
    src = "f('long' 'literal')"
    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == src


def test_main_resolves_issue_with_a_single_invocation(tmpdir):
    path = tmpdir.join('example.py')
    path.write(ISSUE_INPUT)

    assert main((path.strpath,)) == 1
    assert path.read() == ISSUE_EXPECTED

    # A second invocation must have nothing left to rewrite.
    assert main((path.strpath,)) == 0
    assert path.read() == ISSUE_EXPECTED

import timeit
import warnings

import pytest

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def _quiet_tokenize(tokenizer, token):
    """Unknown characters intentionally warn; keep those warnings out of timings."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        return tokenizer.tokenize(token)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("token", "expected"),
    [
        ("justification", ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]),
        ("hello", ["hel", "lo"]),
        ("a", ["a"]),
        ("bc", ["bc"]),
        ("99", ["99"]),
        (".", ["."]),
        ("", [""]),
    ],
)
def test_basic_tokenization_and_edge_cases(token, expected):
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    assert _quiet_tokenize(tokenizer, token) == expected


def test_numeric_tokens_do_not_accumulate_vowels_or_change_later_results():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
    original_phoneme_map = tokenizer.phoneme_map.copy()

    numeric_tokens = ("99", "123", "9876543210", "42", "0123456789" * 20)
    for _ in range(5):
        for token in numeric_tokens:
            syllables = _quiet_tokenize(tokenizer, token)
            assert isinstance(syllables, list)
            assert "".join(syllables) == token
            # Tokenization must not make every subsequent call more expensive.
            assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    assert tokenizer.phoneme_map == original_phoneme_map
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
        "jus",
        "ti",
        "fi",
        "ca",
        "tion",
    ]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("hello") == ["hel", "lo"]


def test_repeated_numeric_results_are_stable():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    first = _quiet_tokenize(tokenizer, "1234567890")

    for _ in range(20):
        assert _quiet_tokenize(tokenizer, "1234567890") == first

    # A reused tokenizer should behave like a fresh one, without learned digits.
    fresh = SyllableTokenizer()
    assert _quiet_tokenize(fresh, "1234567890") == first
    assert fresh.vowels == tokenizer.vowels


def _best_elapsed_time(token, iterations):
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        timer = timeit.Timer(lambda: tokenizer.tokenize(token))
        # The minimum reduces interference from unrelated activity on the test host.
        return min(timer.repeat(repeat=2, number=iterations))


def test_repeated_numbers_are_comparable_in_speed_to_words():
    iterations = 500
    numbers_time = _best_elapsed_time("99", iterations)
    words_time = _best_elapsed_time("thisisanextremelylongword", iterations)

    # This is deliberately a loose bound, not a microbenchmark. The unfixed
    # tokenizer's growing vowel regexp makes this ratio grow dramatically with
    # the iteration count, whereas a linear implementation stays comparable.
    assert numbers_time < words_time * 10, (
        f"Tokenizing {iterations} numeric tokens took {numbers_time:.4f}s, "
        f"versus {words_time:.4f}s for words; numeric tokenization still "
        "shows the reported slowdown"
    )

"""Tests for loading custom version schemes directly from importable modules."""

from pathlib import Path
from textwrap import dedent

from setuptools_scm import Configuration
from setuptools_scm.version import format_version
from setuptools_scm.version import meta
from setuptools_scm.version import no_guess_dev_version


def _render(config: Configuration, tag: str = "1.2.3", **kwargs) -> str:
    scm_version = meta(tag, config=config, **kwargs)
    return format_version(scm_version, **config.__dict__)


def _write_module(root: Path, relative_name: str, source: str) -> None:
    path = root / relative_name
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(dedent(source), encoding="utf-8")


def test_pyproject_schemes_accept_qualified_names(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Schemes must work before the project and its entry points are installed."""
    _write_module(
        tmp_path,
        "qualified_schemes/__init__.py",
        "",
    )
    _write_module(
        tmp_path,
        "qualified_schemes/schemes.py",
        """
        def version_scheme(version):
            return f"{version.tag}.post{version.distance}"

        def local_scheme(version):
            return "+dirty" if version.dirty else ""
        """,
    )
    (tmp_path / "pyproject.toml").write_text(
        dedent(
            """
            [tool.setuptools_scm]
            version_scheme = "qualified_schemes.schemes:version_scheme"
            local_scheme = "qualified_schemes.schemes:local_scheme"
            """
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    config = Configuration.from_file(tmp_path / "pyproject.toml")

    assert _render(config, distance=2, dirty=True) == "1.2.3.post2+dirty"


def test_qualified_names_work_in_scheme_fallback_lists(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _write_module(
        tmp_path,
        "listed_qualified_schemes.py",
        """
        def skip(version):
            return None

        def selected(version):
            return "9.8.7"
        """,
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    config = Configuration(
        version_scheme=[
            "listed_qualified_schemes:skip",
            "listed_qualified_schemes:selected",
        ],
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert _render(config) == "9.8.7"


def test_entry_point_scheme_names_remain_supported():
    """A plain entry-point name must not be mistaken for a qualified name."""
    local_scheme = lambda version: ""
    config = Configuration(
        version_scheme="no-guess-dev",
        local_scheme=local_scheme,
    )
    callable_config = Configuration(
        version_scheme=no_guess_dev_version,
        local_scheme=local_scheme,
    )

    # Compare resolution mechanisms rather than depending on the formatting
    # details of this built-in scheme.
    assert _render(config, distance=0) == _render(callable_config, distance=0)


def test_callable_schemes_remain_supported():
    config = Configuration(
        version_scheme=lambda version: f"callable-{version.tag}",
        local_scheme=lambda version: "+local",
    )

    assert _render(config) == "callable-1.2.3+local"

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src
from add_trailing_comma import main


ISSUE_SRC = (
    "f('long'\n"
    "  'literal')"
)
ISSUE_EXPECTED = (
    "f(\n"
    "    'long'\n"
    "    'literal',\n"
    ")"
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        # The exact example from the issue.
        (ISSUE_SRC, ISSUE_EXPECTED),
        # An existing trailing comma must not be duplicated.
        (
            "f('long'\n"
            "  'literal',)",
            ISSUE_EXPECTED,
        ),
        # The argument can also be a keyword argument.
        (
            "f(value='long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            "f(\n"
            "    value='long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # Calls are not limited to a bare NAME.
        (
            "obj.f('long'\n"
            "      'literal')",
            "obj.f(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        (
            "get_f()('long'\n"
            "        'literal')",
            "get_f()(\n"
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ")",
        ),
        # Indentation is relative to the statement containing the call.
        (
            "def g():\n"
            "    f('long'\n"
            "      'literal')",
            "def g():\n"
            "    f(\n"
            "        'long'\n"
            "        'literal',\n"
            "    )",
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_string_call_fixed_in_one_pass(src, expected):
    actual = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)
    assert actual == expected

    # A correctly resolved call is stable on subsequent passes.
    assert _fix_src(actual, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_parenthesized_string_after_keyword_is_not_a_call():
    # Adding a comma here would change the expression into a tuple and change
    # the meaning of `not`.
    src = (
        "x = not ('long'\n"
        "         'literal')"
    )
    expected = (
        "x = not (\n"
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal'\n"
        ")"
    )
    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_single_line_implicit_string_concatenation_is_unchanged():
    src = "f('long' 'literal')"
    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == src


def test_main_rewrites_issue_example_only_once(tmpdir):
    f = tmpdir.join('f.py')
    f.write(ISSUE_SRC)

    assert main((f.strpath,)) == 1
    assert f.read() == ISSUE_EXPECTED

    # The first invocation must have done all the necessary rewriting.
    assert main((f.strpath,)) == 0
    assert f.read() == ISSUE_EXPECTED

import timeit
import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def _tokenize_without_warnings(tokenizer, token):
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        return tokenizer.tokenize(token)


def test_documented_syllabification_is_preserved():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    assert tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("hello") == ["hel", "lo"]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("foobar-like") == ["foo", "bar", "-", "li", "ke"]

    # Tokens with at most one known vowel, including degenerate inputs, should
    # continue to be returned intact.
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("a") == ["a"]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("bc") == ["bc"]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize(".") == ["."]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("") == [""]


def test_numeric_and_unknown_tokens_do_not_mutate_tokenizer_configuration():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
    original_phoneme_map = tokenizer.phoneme_map.copy()

    # Unknown characters used to be appended to self.vowels on every call.
    # Besides being an unexpected side effect, that made later calls do more
    # work than earlier ones. Include repeated, mixed, punctuated, and non-ASCII
    # inputs so that only special-casing "99" cannot satisfy the test.
    tokens = ("99", "9", "123", "999", "test123", "99.99", "é9")

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for token in tokens:
            first_result = tokenizer.tokenize(token)
            assert "".join(first_result) == token

            for _ in range(10):
                assert tokenizer.tokenize(token) == first_result

    assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels
    assert tokenizer.phoneme_map == original_phoneme_map


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_is_comparable_to_word_tokenization():
    iterations = 1000

    def measure(token):
        # Use a fresh tokenizer for each measurement, as in the issue report.
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
            return timeit.timeit(
                lambda: tokenizer.tokenize(token),
                number=iterations,
            )

    numbers_time = measure("99")
    words_time = measure("thisisanextremelylongword")

    # This is deliberately a loose bound, not a microbenchmark requiring numbers
    # to be faster. With the accumulating-vowels bug, increasing the iteration
    # count makes this ratio grow dramatically (over 100 in the issue report).
    # A linear implementation should leave the two workloads broadly comparable.
    assert numbers_time < words_time * 15, (
        f"Repeated numeric tokenization is still disproportionately slow: "
        f"numbers={numbers_time:.4f}s, words={words_time:.4f}s "
        f"for {iterations} calls"
    )

import pytest

from jwt.api_jwt import PyJWT
from jwt.exceptions import InvalidAudienceError, MissingRequiredClaimError


SECRET = "secret"
ALGORITHMS = ["HS256"]


@pytest.fixture
def jwt():
    return PyJWT()


def test_null_audience_is_ignored_when_no_audience_is_expected(jwt):
    payload = {"some": "payload", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, SECRET, algorithm="HS256")

    decoded = jwt.decode(token, SECRET, algorithms=ALGORITHMS)

    # Ignoring the claim for validation must not remove it from the payload.
    assert decoded == payload
    assert "aud" in decoded
    assert decoded["aud"] is None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("audience", ["urn:me", ["urn:me"]])
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "payload",
    [
        {"some": "payload"},
        {"some": "payload", "aud": None},
    ],
)
def test_null_audience_behaves_like_missing_claim_when_audience_is_expected(
    jwt, payload, audience
):
    token = jwt.encode(payload, SECRET, algorithm="HS256")

    # The issue requires null to be treated exactly like an unspecified aud
    # claim. An absent aud claim raises MissingRequiredClaimError here, so a
    # null aud claim must do the same rather than fail claim-format validation.
    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            SECRET,
            audience=audience,
            algorithms=ALGORITHMS,
        )

    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "payload",
    [
        {"some": "payload"},
        {"some": "payload", "aud": None},
    ],
)
def test_null_audience_does_not_satisfy_required_aud_claim(jwt, payload):
    token = jwt.encode(payload, SECRET, algorithm="HS256")

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            SECRET,
            algorithms=ALGORITHMS,
            options={"require": ["aud"]},
        )

"""Tests for loading custom version schemes directly from qualified names."""

from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion
from setuptools_scm.version import format_version


def _format_with_schemes(version_scheme, local_scheme="no-local-version"):
    config = {
        "version_scheme": version_scheme,
        "local_scheme": local_scheme,
    }
    return format_version(ScmVersion("1.2.3", config=config))


def test_version_scheme_loads_function_from_module_without_entrypoint(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    """A scheme in importable project source must not require installation."""
    (tmp_path / "ttg_custom_version_scheme.py").write_text(
        "def scheme(version):\n"
        "    return f'{version.tag}.post7'\n"
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    result = _format_with_schemes("ttg_custom_version_scheme:scheme")

    assert result == "1.2.3.post7"


def test_version_scheme_supports_nested_package_module(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    package = tmp_path / "ttg_qualified_schemes"
    package.mkdir()
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("")
    (package / "schemes.py").write_text(
        "def main_version(version):\n"
        "    return '2.3.4'\n"
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    result = _format_with_schemes("ttg_qualified_schemes.schemes:main_version")

    assert result == "2.3.4"


def test_local_scheme_also_accepts_qualified_name(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    (tmp_path / "ttg_custom_local_scheme.py").write_text(
        "def local(version):\n"
        "    return '+from.source'\n"
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    result = _format_with_schemes(
        version_scheme=lambda version: "1.2.3",
        local_scheme="ttg_custom_local_scheme:local",
    )

    assert result == "1.2.3+from.source"


def test_qualified_names_work_in_scheme_fallback_lists(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Each string in a scheme list needs qualified-name resolution."""
    (tmp_path / "ttg_scheme_variants.py").write_text(
        "def skip(version):\n"
        "    return None\n"
        "\n"
        "def selected(version):\n"
        "    return '4.5.6'\n"
    )
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))

    result = _format_with_schemes(
        [
            "ttg_scheme_variants:skip",
            "ttg_scheme_variants:selected",
        ]
    )

    assert result == "4.5.6"


def test_plain_entrypoint_scheme_names_remain_supported():
    """Adding qualified names must not break existing entry-point schemes."""
    result = _format_with_schemes("post-release")

    assert result == "1.2.3"

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
from __future__ import absolute_import
from __future__ import unicode_literals

import pytest

from add_trailing_comma import _fix_src
from add_trailing_comma import main


ISSUE_INPUT = (
    "f('long'\n"
    "  'literal')"
)
ISSUE_OUTPUT = (
    'f(\n'
    "    'long'\n"
    "    'literal',\n"
    ')'
)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ('src', 'expected'),
    (
        # The example from the issue must be completely fixed in one pass.
        (ISSUE_INPUT, ISSUE_OUTPUT),
        # The intermediate output shown in the issue should also converge
        # immediately to the same final output.
        (
            'f(\n'
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal'\n"
            ')',
            ISSUE_OUTPUT,
        ),
        # Multiline implicit string concatenation is not limited to simple
        # names or to calls at the start of a line.
        (
            "obj.f('long'\n"
            "      'literal')",
            'obj.f(\n'
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ')',
        ),
        (
            "foo()('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            'foo()(\n'
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ')',
        ),
        (
            "callbacks[0]('long'\n"
            "  'literal')",
            'callbacks[0](\n'
            "    'long'\n"
            "    'literal',\n"
            ')',
        ),
        (
            'if condition:\n'
            "    f('long'\n"
            "      'literal')",
            'if condition:\n'
            '    f(\n'
            "        'long'\n"
            "        'literal',\n"
            '    )',
        ),
    ),
)
def test_multiline_string_call_fixed_in_one_pass(src, expected):
    actual = _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False)
    assert actual == expected
    # A second pass must not be needed to finish or correct the rewrite.
    assert _fix_src(actual, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_parenthesized_string_after_not_is_not_a_function_call():
    # A trailing comma here would turn the string into a one-element tuple and
    # change the meaning of the expression.  The parentheses may be unhugged,
    # but no comma may be introduced.
    src = (
        "x = not ('long'\n"
        "        'literal')"
    )
    expected = (
        'x = not (\n'
        "    'long'\n"
        "    'literal'\n"
        ')'
    )
    assert _fix_src(src, py35_plus=False) == expected


def test_main_resolves_issue_example_with_one_invocation(tmpdir):
    f = tmpdir.join('f.py')
    f.write(ISSUE_INPUT)

    assert main((f.strpath,)) == 1
    assert f.read() == ISSUE_OUTPUT
    assert main((f.strpath,)) == 0
    assert f.read() == ISSUE_OUTPUT

"""Tests for using importable scheme functions without installed entry points."""

import importlib

import setuptools_scm
from setuptools_scm import get_version
from setuptools_scm.version import ScmVersion


entrypoints = importlib.import_module("setuptools_scm._entrypoints")


def _stub_scm_version(monkeypatch):
    """Isolate scheme resolution from the need for a real Git/Hg checkout."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        setuptools_scm,
        "_do_parse",
        lambda config: ScmVersion("1.2.3", config=config),
    )


def _make_importable(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    # This only makes the project's source importable. It does not install a
    # distribution or register any of its entry points.
    monkeypatch.syspath_prepend(str(tmp_path))
    importlib.invalidate_caches()


def _without_entry_points(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        entrypoints,
        "iter_entry_points",
        lambda group, name=None: iter(()),
    )


def test_qualified_version_scheme_does_not_need_an_installed_entry_point(
    tmp_path, monkeypatch
):
    package = tmp_path / "ttg_uninstalled_project"
    package.mkdir()
    (package / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (package / "schemes.py").write_text(
        "def version_scheme(version):\n"
        "    assert str(version.tag) == '1.2.3'\n"
        "    return '4.5.6'\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    _make_importable(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    _without_entry_points(monkeypatch)
    _stub_scm_version(monkeypatch)

    result = get_version(
        root=str(tmp_path),
        version_scheme="ttg_uninstalled_project.schemes:version_scheme",
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert result == "4.5.6"


def test_qualified_version_scheme_works_in_a_scheme_list(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    (tmp_path / "ttg_simple_schemes.py").write_text(
        "def version_scheme(version):\n"
        "    return '7.8.9'\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    _make_importable(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    _without_entry_points(monkeypatch)
    _stub_scm_version(monkeypatch)

    result = get_version(
        root=str(tmp_path),
        version_scheme=[
            lambda version: None,
            "ttg_simple_schemes:version_scheme",
        ],
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert result == "7.8.9"


def test_qualified_local_scheme_is_also_importable(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    (tmp_path / "ttg_local_schemes.py").write_text(
        "def local_scheme(version):\n"
        "    return '+qualified'\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    _make_importable(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    _without_entry_points(monkeypatch)
    _stub_scm_version(monkeypatch)

    result = get_version(
        root=str(tmp_path),
        version_scheme=lambda version: "1.2.3",
        local_scheme="ttg_local_schemes:local_scheme",
    )

    assert result == "1.2.3+qualified"


def test_plain_entry_point_scheme_names_remain_supported(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    class FakeEntryPoint:
        name = "ttg-registered-version-scheme"

        def load(self):
            return lambda version: "2.0.0"

    def fake_iter_entry_points(group, name=None):
        if (
            group == "setuptools_scm.version_scheme"
            and name in (None, FakeEntryPoint.name)
        ):
            return iter([FakeEntryPoint()])
        return iter(())

    monkeypatch.setattr(entrypoints, "iter_entry_points", fake_iter_entry_points)
    _stub_scm_version(monkeypatch)

    result = get_version(
        root=str(tmp_path),
        version_scheme=FakeEntryPoint.name,
        local_scheme=lambda version: "",
    )

    assert result == "2.0.0"

    def __new__(cls, value):
        obj = super().__new__(cls, value)
        obj.count_calls = 0
        return obj

    def count(self, *args):
        self.count_calls += 1
        return super().count(*args)


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("token", "expected"),
    [
        # Documented and ordinary word behavior must remain unchanged.
        ("justification", ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]),
        ("hello", ["hel", "lo"]),
        ("foobar-like", ["foo", "bar", "-", "li", "ke"]),
        # Empty, vowel-less, and punctuation-only tokens are edge cases.
        ("", [""]),
        ("a", ["a"]),
        ("bc", ["bc"]),
        (".", ["."]),
        ("@#$%", ["@#$%"]),
        # Unknown non-punctuation characters are still treated as vowels for
        # the current call. These are the pre-fix tokenization results.
        ("99", ["99"]),
        ("123", ["12", "3"]),
        ("hello123", ["hel", "lo1", "2", "3"]),
    ],
)
def test_tokenization_results_are_preserved(token, expected):
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        assert tokenizer.tokenize(token) == expected


def test_numeric_tokens_still_warn_that_they_are_assigned_as_vowels():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="Character not defined in sonority_hierarchy"):
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_does_not_accumulate_vowels():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
    original_phoneme_map = tokenizer.phoneme_map.copy()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for _ in range(25):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
            assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

        # Results must not depend on numeric tokens processed previously.
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("123") == ["12", "3"]
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("hello123") == ["hel", "lo1", "2", "3"]

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels
    assert tokenizer.phoneme_map == original_phoneme_map


def test_repeated_numeric_calls_do_not_do_increasing_amounts_of_work():
    """
    Deterministic regression check for the repeated-call quadratic behavior.

    The old implementation appended two characters to self.vowels on every
    tokenize("99") call and then called token.count once for every accumulated
    entry. Thus the work for an identical call grew with all preceding calls.
    """
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        first = _CountingStr("99")
        assert tokenizer.tokenize(first) == ["99"]

        for _ in range(64):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]

        last = _CountingStr("99")
        assert tokenizer.tokenize(last) == ["99"]

    # Allow substantially more per-call work than the current implementation
    # needs, while rejecting work proportional to the number of earlier calls.
    assert last.count_calls <= max(32, 2 * first.count_calls)


def test_numeric_input_work_does_not_grow_with_token_length():
    def count_calls_for(token):
        tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
        probe = _CountingStr(token)
        with warnings.catch_warnings():
            warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
            tokenizer.tokenize(probe)
        return probe.count_calls

    short_count = count_calls_for("99")
    long_count = count_calls_for("1234567890" * 8)

    # A fresh tokenizer should not require one full-string count operation for
    # every character appended to an ever-growing vowel list.
    assert long_count <= max(32, 2 * short_count)

import uuid

import pytest

import fakeredis


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "client_class",
    [fakeredis.FakeRedis, fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis],

def test_default_clients_do_not_share_state(client_class):
    """Each no-argument client must behave like a fresh Redis server."""
    first = client_class()
    assert first.keys("*") == []

    first.set("a", "1")
    assert first.get("a") == b"1"

    # This is equivalent to a function-scoped pytest fixture creating a new
    # client for the next test.
    second = client_class()
    assert second.keys("*") == []
    assert second.get("a") is None

    second.set("b", "1")
    assert set(second.keys("*")) == {b"b"}

    # Isolation must work in both directions, and the first client's state
    # must remain intact.
    assert first.get("a") == b"1"
    assert first.get("b") is None
    assert set(first.keys("*")) == {b"a"}


def test_explicit_fake_server_still_shares_state():
    """Users can still opt into shared state with an explicit FakeServer."""

from jwt.exceptions import InvalidAudienceError, MissingRequiredClaimError


@pytest.fixture
def jwt():
    return PyJWT()


def test_null_aud_is_ignored_when_no_audience_is_requested(jwt):
    payload = {"some": "payload", "aud": None}
    token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")

    decoded = jwt.decode(token, "secret", algorithms=["HS256"])

    # Ignoring aud during validation must not remove it from the decoded token.
    assert decoded == payload
    assert "aud" in decoded
    assert decoded["aud"] is None


@pytest.mark.parametrize("audience", ["urn:me", ["urn:me", "urn:you"]])
def test_null_aud_is_treated_as_missing_when_audience_is_requested(jwt, audience):
    token = jwt.encode({"some": "payload", "aud": None}, "secret")

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            audience=audience,
            algorithms=["HS256"],
        )

    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("payload", [{"some": "payload"}, {"some": "payload", "aud": None}])
def test_null_aud_behaves_like_an_absent_claim_when_aud_is_required(jwt, payload):
    token = jwt.encode(payload, "secret")

    with pytest.raises(MissingRequiredClaimError) as exc_info:
        jwt.decode(
            token,
            "secret",
            algorithms=["HS256"],
            options={"require": ["aud"]},
        )

    assert exc_info.value.claim == "aud"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("aud", ["", [], 0, False])
def test_other_falsey_aud_values_are_not_treated_as_null(jwt, aud):

            "secret",
            audience="urn:me",
            algorithms=["HS256"],

"""Regression tests for SyllableTokenizer's repeated numeric-token slowdown."""

import warnings

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


def _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, token):
    """Unknown characters are documented to warn and be treated as vowels."""
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        return tokenizer.tokenize(token)


def test_numeric_tokens_do_not_permanently_expand_vowels():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    for _ in range(20):
        assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "99") == [
            "99"
        ]
        assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

    # Other previously unseen characters must not accumulate in the tokenizer's
    # configuration either, including characters in mixed alphanumeric tokens.
    for token in ("123", "test123", "42", "λ7", "Hello99World"):
        _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, token)
        assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_unknown_characters_retain_their_vowel_semantics_within_a_token():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    # These are the syllabifications produced when unknown characters are
    # assigned the maximum sonority value, as assign_values documents. A fix
    # that merely stops updating self.vowels would incorrectly return each
    # token whole because it would no longer recognize these vowels.
    assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "9") == ["9"]
    assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "99") == ["99"]
    assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "123") == [
        "12",
        "3",
    ]
    assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "test123") == [
        "tes",
        "t12",
        "3",
    ]

    # Results must depend on the token, not on how many tokens were processed
    # earlier by this tokenizer instance.
    for _ in range(5):
        assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "123") == [
            "12",
            "3",
        ]
        assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(
            tokenizer, "test123"
        ) == ["tes", "t12", "3"]


class _CountingStr(str):
    """A string that measures the vowel-counting work done by tokenize."""

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.count_calls = 0

    def count(self, *args):
        self.count_calls += 1
        return super().count(*args)


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_has_constant_per_call_scanning_work():
    """Check algorithmic growth deterministically instead of using timings."""
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    token = _CountingStr("99")
    calls_per_tokenization = []

    for _ in range(25):
        before = token.count_calls
        assert _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, token) == [
            "99"
        ]
        calls_per_tokenization.append(token.count_calls - before)

    # In the buggy implementation every call appends two more characters to
    # self.vowels, so this sequence grows on every call and total work is
    # quadratic. A correct implementation may use a different counting
    # strategy (including no str.count calls), but its work cannot keep growing
    # merely because the same token was seen before.
    assert max(calls_per_tokenization) <= calls_per_tokenization[0] + 1


def test_numeric_stress_does_not_change_words_or_edge_case_results():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels

    assert tokenizer.tokenize("") == [""]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize(".") == ["."]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("@#$%") == ["@#$%"]

    for _ in range(30):
        _tokenize_without_unknown_character_warnings(tokenizer, "99")

    # Documented word behavior must remain unchanged after processing numbers.
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
        "jus",
        "ti",
        "fi",
        "ca",
        "tion",
    ]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("hello") == ["hel", "lo"]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("a") == ["a"]
    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels

import uuid

import pytest

import fakeredis


def _unique_key(label):
    return f"issue-299:{label}:{uuid.uuid4().hex}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("client_cls", [fakeredis.FakeRedis, fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis])
def test_default_clients_do_not_persist_state_between_instances(client_cls):
    """Separate default clients, such as separate pytest fixture instances, are isolated."""
    first = client_cls()
    second = client_cls()
    first_key = _unique_key("first")
    second_key = _unique_key("second")

    assert first.set(first_key, "first")

    # A newly constructed client must not inherit the first client's state.
    assert second.get(first_key) is None

    assert second.set(second_key, "second")
    assert second.get(second_key) == b"second"
    assert first.get(first_key) == b"first"

    # Isolation must also apply to writes made by the second client.
    assert first.get(second_key) is None


def test_explicit_fake_server_still_shares_state():
    shared_server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
    first = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=shared_server)
    second = fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis(server=shared_server)
    independent = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=fakeredis.FakeServer())
    key = _unique_key("shared-server")

    first.set(key, "shared")

from streamlink.compat import is_win32

@pytest.mark.skipif(is_win32, reason="POSIX argument-list behavior")
class TestMpvTitleCommandLine(CommandLineTestCase):
    def test_title_with_spaces_is_one_equals_argument(self):
        """The title must not be a separate argument or contain shell quotes."""
        self._test_args(
            [
                "streamlink",
                "-p",
                "/usr/bin/mpv",
                "--title",
                "{title}",
                "http://test.se",
                "test",
            ],
            ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title=Test Title", "-"],
        )

    def test_default_title_uses_equals_syntax(self):
        self._test_args(
            ["streamlink", "-p", "/usr/bin/mpv", "http://test.se", "test"],
            ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title=http://test.se", "-"],
        )

    def test_title_is_added_after_existing_player_arguments(self):
        self._test_args(
            [
                "streamlink",
                "-p",
                "/usr/bin/mpv --cache 2048",
                "--title",
                "{title}",
                "http://test.se",
                "test",
            ],
            [
                "/usr/bin/mpv",
                "--cache",
                "2048",
                "--title=Test Title",
                "-",
            ],
        )


def _create_posix_arguments(player, title):
    output = PlayerOutput(player, title=title, quiet=False)
    return output._create_arguments()


@pytest.mark.skipif(is_win32, reason="POSIX argument-list behavior")
@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title,expected_title",
    [
        ("Test Title", "Test Title"),
        ("  leading and trailing spaces  ", "  leading and trailing spaces  "),
        ("it's a \"quoted\" title", "it's a \"quoted\" title"),
        (u"Tѥst Āuƭhǿr", u"Tѥst Āuƭhǿr"),
        ("", ""),
        # Property expansion still needs mpv escaping, but subprocess does
        # not invoke a shell and therefore must not receive shlex quotes.
        ("cost $5", "cost $$5"),
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_a_single_literal_argv_value(title, expected_title):
    assert _create_posix_arguments("/usr/bin/mpv", title) == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title=" + expected_title,
        "-",
    ]


@pytest.mark.skipif(is_win32, reason="POSIX argument-list behavior")
def test_mpv_without_a_title_does_not_add_a_title_option():

    assert output._create_arguments() == ["/usr/bin/mpv", "-"]

        "Test Title",
        "-",
    ]


def test_windows_command_line_does_not_contain_posix_shell_quotes():
    """Windows argument quoting belongs to list2cmdline, not shlex.quote."""
    with patch("streamlink_cli.output.is_win32", new=True), patch(
        "streamlink_cli.output.os.path.basename", new=ntpath.basename
    ):
        output = PlayerOutput(r"C:\mpv\mpv.exe", title="Test Title", quiet=False)
        command = output._create_arguments()

    if isinstance(command, bytes):
        command = command.decode(get_filesystem_encoding())

    assert command == r'C:\mpv\mpv.exe "--title=Test Title" -'

import time
import warnings

import pytest

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


DEFAULT_VOWELS = "aeiouy"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("token", "expected"),
    [
        ("justification", ["jus", "ti", "fi", "ca", "tion"]),
        ("hello", ["hel", "lo"]),
        ("programming", ["pro", "gram", "ming"]),
        ("foobar-like", ["foo", "bar", "-", "li", "ke"]),
        ("a", ["a"]),
        ("bc", ["bc"]),
        (".", ["."]),
        ("", [""]),
    ],
)
def test_ordinary_syllabification_is_unchanged(token, expected):
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    assert tokenizer.tokenize(token) == expected
    assert tokenizer.vowels == DEFAULT_VOWELS


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("token", "expected"),
    [
        ("9", ["9"]),
        ("99", ["99"]),
        # Unknown characters are assigned vowel sonority for the current token.
        # These are the results of the original algorithm on its first call.
        ("123", ["12", "3"]),
        ("hello123", ["hel", "lo1", "2", "3"]),
        # The fix should apply to all unknown characters, not just ASCII digits.
        ("ββ", ["ββ"]),
    ],
)
def test_unknown_characters_do_not_permanently_become_vowels(token, expected):
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        result = tokenizer.tokenize(token)

    assert result == expected
    assert "".join(result) == token
    assert tokenizer.vowels == DEFAULT_VOWELS


def test_numeric_results_are_independent_of_call_history():
    tokens = ("99", "123", "987654321", "hello123")
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        first_results = {token: tokenizer.tokenize(token) for token in tokens}

        for _ in range(25):
            for token, expected in first_results.items():
                assert tokenizer.tokenize(token) == expected

    assert tokenizer.vowels == DEFAULT_VOWELS

    # A fresh tokenizer and a heavily reused one must produce the same results.
    fresh_tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for token, expected in first_results.items():
            assert fresh_tokenizer.tokenize(token) == expected

    assert fresh_tokenizer.vowels == DEFAULT_VOWELS


def test_long_numeric_token_does_not_grow_tokenizer_state():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    token = "0123456789" * 20

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        syllables = tokenizer.tokenize(token)

    assert syllables
    assert all(syllable for syllable in syllables)
    assert "".join(syllables) == token
    assert tokenizer.vowels == DEFAULT_VOWELS


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_remains_fast():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)

        # Fail deterministically and quickly on the original state-growing bug.
        assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        assert tokenizer.vowels == DEFAULT_VOWELS

        started = time.perf_counter()
        for _ in range(1500):
            assert tokenizer.tokenize("99") == ["99"]
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started

    # This is a generous ceiling for a linear implementation, which normally
    # takes only a small fraction of a second. The quadratic implementation
    # takes several seconds at this iteration count and grows self.vowels on
    # every call.
    assert elapsed < 2.0, (
        f"1500 numeric tokenizations took {elapsed:.3f}s; "
        "numeric tokenization may still scale quadratically"
    )
    assert tokenizer.vowels == DEFAULT_VOWELS

    first = client_class()
    second = client_class()

    assert first.keys("*") == []
    assert second.keys("*") == []

    first.set("issue-299:a", "1")
    assert first.get("issue-299:a") == b"1"
    assert second.get("issue-299:a") is None

    second.set("issue-299:b", "1")
    assert first.get("issue-299:b") is None
    assert first.keys("*") == [b"issue-299:a"]
    assert second.keys("*") == [b"issue-299:b"]


def test_default_sync_client_is_isolated_from_default_async_client():
    """A default synchronous client must not use the async default server."""

    async def exercise():
        async_client = aioredis.FakeRedis()
        sync_client = fakeredis.FakeRedis()
        try:
            await async_client.set("issue-299:async-default", "value")
            assert sync_client.get("issue-299:async-default") is None

            sync_client.set("issue-299:sync-default", "value")
            assert await async_client.get("issue-299:sync-default") is None
        finally:
            await async_client.connection_pool.disconnect()

    asyncio.run(exercise())


def test_explicit_fake_server_still_shares_state():
    """Isolation must not remove the supported explicit sharing mechanism."""
    shared_server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
    first = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=shared_server)
    second = fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis(server=shared_server)
    separate = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=fakeredis.FakeServer())

    first.set("issue-299:shared", "value")

    assert second.get("issue-299:shared") == b"value"
    assert separate.get("issue-299:shared") is None

    second.set("issue-299:written-by-second", "value")
    assert first.get("issue-299:written-by-second") == b"value"

def test_numeric_and_mixed_tokens_are_repeatable_and_lossless(token):

    with warnings.catch_warnings():

        first = tokenizer.tokenize(token)
        second = tokenizer.tokenize(token)

    assert "".join(first) == token
    assert all(isinstance(syllable, str) for syllable in first)

    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for token in tokens:

    used_tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for _ in range(20):
            used_tokenizer.tokenize("99")

        for token in ("99", "123", "999999999", "test123", "Hello99World"):
            fresh_tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
            expected = fresh_tokenizer.tokenize(token)

def _elapsed_repeated_tokenization(token, iterations):
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

        return timeit.timeit(

            number=iterations,

        "Repeated numeric tokenization degraded disproportionately: "
        f"numbers={number_time:.4f}s, words={word_time:.4f}s "
        f"for {iterations} calls"
    )

import unittest

import pytest

from streamlink.compat import is_win32
from streamlink.utils.encoding import maybe_decode
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput
from tests.mock import patch
from tests.test_cmdline import CommandLineTestCase


posix_only = pytest.mark.skipif(is_win32, reason="POSIX argv construction")


@unittest.skipIf(is_win32, "test only applicable on POSIX")
class TestMpvTitleCommandLine(CommandLineTestCase):
    def test_explicit_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax(self):
        self._test_args(
            ["streamlink", "-p", "/usr/bin/mpv", "--title", "{title}",
             "http://test.se", "test"],
            ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title=Test Title", "-"]
        )

    def test_default_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax(self):
        self._test_args(
            ["streamlink", "-p", "/usr/bin/mpv", "http://test.se", "test"],
            ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title=http://test.se", "-"]
        )


@posix_only
@pytest.mark.parametrize("title", [
    "Test Title",
    "",
    "  leading and trailing whitespace  ",
    "single ' and double \" quotes",
    u"Tѥst Āuƭhǿr",
    "shell ; metacharacters & *must* remain literal",
])
def test_mpv_title_is_one_unquoted_argv_entry(title):
    output = PlayerOutput("/usr/bin/mpv", title=title, quiet=False)

    # Popen receives an argv list on POSIX, not a shell command. Shell quotes
    # would therefore become literal characters in the title shown by mpv.
    assert output._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title=" + title,
        "-",
    ]


@posix_only
def test_mpv_property_expansion_escaping_is_retained():
    output = PlayerOutput("/usr/bin/mpv", title="Cost $5", quiet=False)

    assert output._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title=Cost $$5",
        "-",
    ]


@posix_only
def test_mpv_title_follows_existing_player_arguments():
    output = PlayerOutput(
        "/usr/bin/mpv --cache 2048",
        title="Test Title",
        quiet=False,
    )

    assert output._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--cache",
        "2048",
        "--title=Test Title",
        "-",
    ]


@posix_only
def test_vlc_title_argument_format_is_unchanged():
    output = PlayerOutput("/usr/bin/vlc", title="Test Title", quiet=False)

    assert output._create_arguments() == [
        "/usr/bin/vlc",
        "--input-title-format",
        "Test Title",
        "-",
    ]


def test_windows_mpv_command_line_does_not_use_posix_shell_quoting():
    with patch("streamlink_cli.output.is_win32", True):
        output = PlayerOutput("mpv", title="Test Title", quiet=False)
        arguments = maybe_decode(output._create_arguments())

    # list2cmdline supplies the Windows quoting needed to keep the value in
    # one argument. POSIX single quotes must not be embedded in mpv's value.
    assert arguments == u'mpv "--title=Test Title" -'

import warnings

import pytest

from nltk.tokenize import SyllableTokenizer


class _CountingStr(str):
    """String that lets us measure per-call work without using wall-clock time."""

    def __new__(cls, value):
        obj = super().__new__(cls, value)
        obj.count_calls = 0
        return obj

    def count(self, *args):
        self.count_calls += 1
        return super().count(*args)


def test_repeated_numeric_tokenization_does_not_accumulate_state_or_work():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
    count_history = []

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for _ in range(20):
            token = _CountingStr("99")
            assert tokenizer.tokenize(token) == ["99"]
            count_history.append(token.count_calls)

    # Unknown characters must not become permanent vowels. In particular, the
    # amount of work for a later call must not grow with the number of calls.
    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels
    assert max(count_history) <= count_history[0]


def test_long_numeric_tokens_are_returned_whole_without_changing_vowels():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()
    original_vowels = tokenizer.vowels
    numeric_tokens = [
        "9" * 200,
        "0123456789" * 20,
        "١٢٣٤٥",  # Non-ASCII digits are unknown characters too.
    ]

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for token in numeric_tokens:
            assert tokenizer.tokenize(token) == [token]

    assert tokenizer.vowels == original_vowels


def test_unknown_character_handling_is_preserved_with_custom_hierarchy():
    hierarchy = ["ae", "ln", "bcd"]
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer(sonority_hierarchy=hierarchy)

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="Character not defined"):
        values = tokenizer.assign_values("7")

    # The character is still assigned vowel-like sonority for this operation,
    # but it must not be saved in the tokenizer's reusable vowel configuration.
    assert values == [("7", max(tokenizer.phoneme_map.values()))]
    assert tokenizer.vowels == hierarchy[0]


def test_numeric_tokens_do_not_affect_subsequent_word_syllabification():
    tokenizer = SyllableTokenizer()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", UserWarning)
        for _ in range(10):
            tokenizer.tokenize("99")

    assert tokenizer.tokenize("justification") == [
        "jus",
        "ti",
        "fi",
        "ca",
        "tion",
    ]
    assert tokenizer.tokenize("foobar-like") == [
        "foo",
        "bar",
        "-",
        "li",
        "ke",
    ]

"""Regression tests for state leaking between independently created clients."""

import uuid

import pytest

import fakeredis


@pytest.mark.parametrize("client_class", [fakeredis.FakeRedis, fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis])
def test_default_sync_clients_have_independent_state(client_class):
    """Each default client must behave like the function-scoped fixture in the issue."""
    first = client_class()
    second = client_class()

    first.set("a", "1")

    # A newly constructed client must not see data written through another one.
    assert second.keys("*") == []
    assert second.get("a") is None

    second.set("b", "1")

    # Isolation must apply in both directions, not just to the new client.
    assert first.get("a") == b"1"
    assert first.get("b") is None
    assert second.get("a") is None
    assert second.get("b") == b"1"
    assert set(first.keys("*")) == {b"a"}
    assert set(second.keys("*")) == {b"b"}


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_default_async_clients_have_independent_state():
    """The asynchronous constructor must not retain the old shared-default behavior."""
    first = fakeredis.FakeAsyncRedis()
    second = fakeredis.FakeAsyncRedis()

    try:
        await first.set("a", "1")

        # This is the asynchronous equivalent of creating a fresh fixture client.
        assert await second.get("a") is None
        assert await second.keys("*") == []

        await second.set("b", "1")

        assert await first.get("a") == b"1"
        assert await first.get("b") is None
        assert await second.get("a") is None
        assert await second.get("b") == b"1"
        assert set(await first.keys("*")) == {b"a"}
        assert set(await second.keys("*")) == {b"b"}
    finally:
        await first.connection_pool.disconnect()
        await second.connection_pool.disconnect()


def test_explicit_fake_server_still_shares_state():
    """Fixing the default must not remove deliberate sharing through FakeServer."""
    server = fakeredis.FakeServer()
    first = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=server)
    second = fakeredis.FakeStrictRedis(server=server)
    unrelated = fakeredis.FakeRedis(server=fakeredis.FakeServer())

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""Regression tests for mpv's required ``--option=value`` syntax."""

import pytest

from streamlink.compat import is_win32
from streamlink_cli.output import PlayerOutput
from tests.test_cmdline import CommandLineTestCase


pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
    is_win32,
    reason="These tests inspect the POSIX argument list passed to subprocess",
)


def create_player_arguments(player, title, player_args=None):
    """Build player arguments without starting a player or opening a stream."""
    kwargs = {"title": title, "quiet": False}
    if player_args is not None:
        kwargs["args"] = player_args
    return PlayerOutput(player, **kwargs)._create_arguments()


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title",
    [
        "Test Title",
        "",
        "https://www.twitch.tv/videos/533706108",
        u"Tѥst Āuƭhǿr",
        "Title with \"double quotes\" and 'single quotes'",
        "  leading and trailing whitespace  ",
        "--a-title-that-looks-like-an-option",
        "a title containing = signs",
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_is_one_equals_argument_without_shell_quoting(title):
    """The title must be attached with '=' and passed verbatim by subprocess.

    PlayerOutput supplies an argv list directly to subprocess, so shell quoting
    would become part of mpv's title rather than protect whitespace.
    """
    assert create_player_arguments("/usr/bin/mpv", title) == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title=" + title,
        "-",
    ]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "title, escaped_title",
    [
        ("Now playing ${title}", "Now playing $${title}"),
        (r"Price: \$5", "Price: $5"),
    ],
)
def test_mpv_title_equals_syntax_preserves_property_escaping(title, escaped_title):
    """Using the new option syntax must not bypass mpv title escaping."""
    assert create_player_arguments("/usr/bin/mpv", title) == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--title=" + escaped_title,
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_title_is_added_after_existing_player_arguments():
    """Mirror the failing command while retaining user-supplied player args."""
    assert create_player_arguments(
        "/usr/bin/mpv --cache 2048", "Test Title"
    ) == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "--cache",
        "2048",
        "--title=Test Title",
        "-",
    ]


def test_mpv_without_a_title_does_not_add_a_title_option():
    assert create_player_arguments("/usr/bin/mpv", None) == [
        "/usr/bin/mpv",
        "-",
    ]


def test_vlc_title_argument_format_is_unchanged():
    """The mpv-specific change must not alter other players' arguments."""
    assert create_player_arguments("/usr/bin/vlc", "Test Title") == [
        "/usr/bin/vlc",
        "--input-title-format",
        "Test Title",
        "-",
    ]


class TestMpvTitleCommandLine(CommandLineTestCase):
    """Exercise the same CLI path used when Streamlink opens the player."""

    def test_explicit_mpv_title_with_spaces(self):
        self._test_args(
            [
                "streamlink",
                "-p",
                "/usr/bin/mpv",
                "--title",
                "{title}",
                "http://test.se",
                "test",
            ],
            ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title=Test Title", "-"],
        )

    def test_default_mpv_title_uses_equals_syntax(self):
        self._test_args(
            ["streamlink", "-p", "/usr/bin/mpv", "http://test.se", "test"],
            ["/usr/bin/mpv", "--title=http://test.se", "-"],
        )

    def test_mpv_title_with_multiple_metadata_fields(self):
        self._test_args(
            [
                "streamlink",
                "-p",
                "/usr/bin/mpv",
                "--title",
                "{title} -- {author}",
                "http://test.se",
                "test",
            ],
            [
                "/usr/bin/mpv",
                u"--title=Test Title -- Tѥst Āuƭhǿr",
                "-",
            ],
        )
